dram:dram.topo.floorplan.statement: On the die the memory shires and their LPDDR4X PHYs form a strip about 1.76 mm wide down each side (1.74 and 1.80 mm); the 6-column shire grid between them spans about 22.2 mm.
dram:dram.topo.floorplan.note: Derived from the published die size and photo geometry, not from a floorplan document.

dram:dram.topo.pll.statement: The boot firmware programs the memory PLL in memory shire 0 and memory shire 4 only: one PLL per side.
dram:dram.topo.pll.note: How the clock reaches memory shires 1-3 and 5-7 is not described; presumably distributed along each side.

dram:dram.addr.memshire.statement: The memory shire that serves a line is picked by physical-address bits 8:6, so consecutive 64-byte lines rotate over the eight memory shires; the memory shire's read counter confirmed the bits for 64 of 64 lines in every one of 15 passes on three cards.
dram:dram.addr.memshire.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:21 (`MEMSHIRE_SEL_ADDR_RANGE 8:6`); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.26 §1.4.3 ('the Memory Shire is selected by the NoC using bits [8:6] by default'); external/et-platform/device-minion-runtime/tools/zebumem.c:68-72; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json [item=MEM-P3].per_card.<card>.tests.P3_msmap_match (64 of 64 lines per pass); anatomy page §4
dram:dram.addr.memshire.note: Measured as well as specified. PA[8:6] are the low three bits of the L3 home shire's PA[10:6], so memory shire m serves home shires m, m+8, m+16, m+24.

dram:dram.addr.channel.statement: Inside the memory shire, physical-address bit 9 picks the controller (the channel): the memory shire's control register resets with its controller-select bit field at 9 and both controllers enabled, and the default boot never rewrites it. The two channels alternate every 512 bytes.
dram:dram.addr.channel.source: external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:22 (`MEMSHIRE_MCTL_SEL_ADDR_RANGE 9`); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/ms_regs.h:160 (MS_REGS_MS_MEM_CTL_RESET_VALUE 0x000307f1892481c6: esr_ms_addr_mc_bit_sel = 9, esr_ms_mc_en = 3; fields at ms_regs.h:489-600); external/core-et/rtl/inc/esr_defines.vh:149-158 (ESR_MS_MEM_CTL_RESET_VAL); only the reduced-memory-shire path writes ms_mem_ctl (external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/noc_configuration.c:294-313); zebumem.c:72 ('addr[9] controller (0=even, 1=odd)')
dram:dram.addr.channel.note: Upgrades the earlier inference from a tool comment (counters-and-dram.md §3.4, chip-diagram fact L50): the reset value is in the SoC's own register header. Latency cannot see this bit: flipping it, like flipping a bank bit, lets the second load ride along (memprobe summary.json bits['9'].b_minus_b0_med = 0).

dram:dram.addr.strip.statement: Before a request reaches its controller, the memory shire removes physical-address bits 9:6 (the memory-shire and channel bits), so each controller sees its own lines as one contiguous address space.

dram:dram.addr.addrmap.statement: The controllers' address map as programmed (ECC off): column bits 4:0 = HIF 4:0, bank bits 2:0 = HIF 7:5, column bits 9:5 = HIF 12:8, row bits 16:0 = HIF 29:13 (HIF is the controller's internal address in 16-bit words).
dram:dram.addr.addrmap.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4639-4654 (ADDRMAP1 0x00030303, ADDRMAP2 0x03000000, ADDRMAP3 0x03030303, ADDRMAP5-6 0x07070707, ADDRMAP7 0x00000f07); field meanings and internal bases from external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html (ADDRMAP1-7); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md §3.4
dram:dram.addr.addrmap.note: Register values are from the firmware source; the running cards' registers have not been read back (the hub's ask-memshire). The 32 GB ECC branch (:4590-4626) is not taken: ECC is off.

dram:dram.addr.pa-map.statement: In physical-address terms, inside one channel: bank = PA[12:10] (8 banks), column = PA[17:13] and PA[5:1] (1,024 columns of 16 bits, a 2 KB page), row = PA[34:18] (17 bits). A 64-byte line is two 32-byte BL16 bursts from one row; PA[5] picks the half.
dram:dram.addr.pa-map.source: derived from dram.addr.strip and dram.addr.addrmap (HIF = controller byte address / 2 for a 16-bit channel); measured by flipping one bit: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json bits['13'..'17'].b_minus_b0_med = -12 (same row), bits['18'..'29'] = +9 (other row), bits['6'..'12'] ~ 0; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P4; anatomy page §5 #which-address-bits-share-a-row; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md §3.4
dram:dram.addr.pa-map.note: Bank and row bits are measured (a same-bank, other-row pair conflicts from bit 18 up on three cards); the split of PA[12:10] into bank rather than channel or column is from the programmed map. zebumem.c:74-111 prints a different swizzle, but only 'if using DDR DRAM models' (an emulation model), and silicon disagrees with it.

dram:dram.addr.interleave.statement: Consequences of the map: 64-byte lines rotate over the 8 memory shires, the 2 channels of each alternate every 512 B, a channel sees one line per 1 KB and puts consecutive lines of its own in consecutive banks, a bank's row holds 32 lines spaced 8 KB apart, and a 256 KB aligned block touches one row in each of the 128 channel-banks.
dram:dram.addr.interleave.source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:352-371 (§3.4); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md '## Rows' (sequential: next bank, 32 columns per row visit)

dram:dram.addr.region.statement: DRAM starts at physical address 0x80_0000_0000; minions reach only the 'Low' view, and device allocations come back as 0x80_xxxx_xxxx addresses.
dram:dram.addr.region.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.551 (Table 15-96) and p.553 (Table 15-98); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:348-350, 379

dram:dram.org.capacity.statement: 32 GB of LPDDR4X on the V3 cards (a Micron part): 2 GB, i.e. 16 Gbit, per channel; the chip supports up to 32 GB 'using LPDDR4X at 16 Gbits per channel'.
dram:dram.org.capacity.source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.1 ('32GB (Micron part) v3 card'); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1; external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:389-398 (MR8 density decode to 32 GB)

dram:dram.org.geometry.statement: Each channel is one rank of 8 banks x 131,072 rows x 2 KB pages (1,024 columns of 16 bits): 8 x 131,072 x 2 KB = 2 GB, matching the capacity. One activate therefore senses 16,384 bits into one bank's sense amplifiers.
dram:dram.org.geometry.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4639-4654 (3 bank, 10 column, 17 row address bits); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:38 (`DDR_BANKS_SIZE 3`); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4539 (ODTMAP rank 0 only); JEDEC JESD209-4 addressing for a 16 Gb-per-channel LPDDR4 die (8 banks, R0-R16, C0-C9, 2 KB page)
dram:dram.org.geometry.note: The geometry is what the programmed map and the capacity require and what JEDEC specifies for this density (GENERIC); the part's datasheet, which would confirm it, is not in the sources.

dram:dram.org.line-vs-page.statement: A 64-byte line uses 512 of the 16,384 bits an activate senses: 1/32 of the open row. The other 31 lines of that row (8 KB apart in the address space) can then be read as row hits until the row closes.

dram:dram.org.part.statement: The exact LPDDR4X part (Micron part number), its die density, the number of dies per package and whether each channel is one x16 die or two byte-mode dies are not in any source. The firmware reads the vendor (MR5; Micron = 0xFF) and density (MR8) at every boot and logs them, but no log has been captured.
dram:dram.org.part.source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf p.1; external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:364-398 (ddr_config: 'DRAM vendor = MICRON', 'DRAM size = 32GB'); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/utils/mem_controller_utils.c:936-1027 (ms_verify_ddr_density; comment 'for the micron part it is 0x10 for 32gb and 0x18 for 64gb')
dram:dram.org.part.note: The firmware labels MR8 density code 6 '64gb/32GB' (mem_controller_utils.c:1000-1004); in JEDEC LPDDR4 terms code 6 is 32 Gb per die, 16 Gb per channel (GENERIC), which fits 2 GB per channel.

dram:dram.org.die-internals.statement: The die's internal organisation below the bank (subarrays or mats, cells per bitline, open or folded bitlines, sense-amplifier variant, wordline boost and array voltages, cell capacitance, process node) is vendor-proprietary and appears in no ET source; the diagram's transistor level is therefore JEDEC/textbook GENERIC.
dram:dram.org.die-internals.source: none (absence noted across external/et-man, external/core-et, external/et-platform)

dram:dram.ctl.clock.statement: The firmware hard-codes the '933 MHz' DDR mode on every card: the controller (DFI) clock is 933 MHz and runs 1:2 with the DRAM clock, so the DRAM clock is 1,866 MHz and the data rate 3,733 MT/s, not the datasheet's 4,266. Telemetry reads mhz.ddr = 933 in every sample.
dram:dram.ctl.clock.source: external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:643-649 (DDR_FREQUENCY_933MHZ, '//TODO: decide ddr_mode'); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:768 (DfiFreqRatio_p0=1), :4536 (MSTR 0x00080020: lpddr4=1, burst_rdwr=8 = BL16); docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace2-telemetry.jsonl field mhz.ddr
dram:dram.ctl.clock.note: One DFI clock = 1.071 ns, one DRAM clock tCK = 0.536 ns; timings below convert DFI clocks to ns. At 600 MHz one minion cycle is 1.667 ns.

dram:dram.ctl.peak-bw.statement: At 3,733 MT/s a 16-bit channel peaks at 7.47 GB/s, a memory shire at 14.9 GB/s and the chip at 119.5 GB/s; at the datasheet's 4,266 MT/s the chip would reach 136.5 GB/s.
dram:dram.ctl.peak-bw.source: arithmetic: 2 B x 3.733 GT/s; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.4 §1 (4,266 MT/s, printed '133 Gbytes/s')

dram:dram.ctl.noc-headroom.statement: Each memory shire's NoC side (32 GB/s) is 2.1x its DRAM side at the programmed rate (14.9 GB/s).
dram:dram.ctl.noc-headroom.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1.1; dram.ctl.peak-bw

dram:dram.ctl.measured-bw.statement: Streaming from DRAM the whole chip reaches 76 GB/s at 600 MHz (64% of 119.5); tensor stores to DRAM also reach 76 GB/s, stores through the L1 27 GB/s.
dram:dram.ctl.measured-bw.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'Bandwidth at 600 MHz, 1,024 minions' (E33, E29); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table rows 'Tensor load from DRAM', 'fsw.ps stores to DRAM through the L1'

dram:dram.ctl.page-policy.statement: Open-page policy: the controller keeps a bank's row open until it must close it (another row of that bank, or a refresh); no page-close timer, no auto-precharge.
dram:dram.ctl.page-policy.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4661-4664 (SCHED 0x00a01f01: pageclose=0; SCHED1 pageclose_timer=0), :4668 (PCCFG 0); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/driver/mem_controller.c:245 (config_auto_precharge = 0); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 (ddrc_main_ctl: read/write auto-precharge, high/low priority); meaning of pageclose=0 from external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html (SCHED.pageclose: 'the bank remains open until there is a need to close it ... also known as open page policy')
dram:dram.ctl.page-policy.note: Measured: 96% of loads whose previous load came after the last refresh were row hits, 4% across a refresh (anatomy §5; 95-96% vs 3-4% on three cards).

dram:dram.ctl.tRCD.statement: Activate-to-read delay tRCD = 17 DFI clocks = 18.2 ns (10.9 minion cycles at 600 MHz).
dram:dram.ctl.tRCD.note: Measured: an open-row hit saves 11-12 cycles (dram.lat.row-hit).

dram:dram.ctl.tRP.statement: Precharge time tRP = 17 DFI clocks = 18.2 ns (10.9 cycles).
dram:dram.ctl.tRP.note: Measured: a load to another row of the bank just used pays about 9-10 cycles more (dram.lat.row-sequential).

dram:dram.ctl.tRAS-tRC.statement: Minimum row-open time tRAS = 40 DFI clocks = 42.9 ns; row cycle tRC (activate to activate in one bank) = 59 DFI clocks = 63.2 ns (37.9 cycles).
dram:dram.ctl.tRAS-tRC.note: tRC matches the measured back-to-back row-conflict penalty (+36.5 to +38.5 cycles, dram.lat.row-conflict).

dram:dram.ctl.RL-WL.statement: Read latency RL = 18 DFI clocks = 36 DRAM clocks = 19.3 ns (read DBI on); write latency WL = 8 DFI = 16 DRAM clocks = 8.6 ns.

dram:dram.ctl.burst.statement: Burst length 16 on a 16-bit channel: one READ returns 32 bytes in 8 DRAM clocks (4.3 ns, tCCD = 4 DFI clocks), so a 64-byte line takes two READs to the same row.

dram:dram.ctl.tRRD-tFAW.statement: Activate-to-activate in different banks tRRD = 10 DFI = 10.7 ns; at most four activates per rolling tFAW = 38 DFI = 40.7 ns per channel.

dram:dram.ctl.tWR.statement: Write recovery: MR1 = 0x64 sets nWR = 34 DRAM clocks (18.2 ns); write-to-precharge wr2pre = 30 DFI clocks, read-to-precharge rd2pre = 8.

dram:dram.ctl.dbi.statement: Data-bus inversion is on for reads and writes, and data masking is enabled: the controller's DBICTL sets rd_dbi_en, wr_dbi_en and dm_en.
dram:dram.ctl.dbi.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4522 (DBICTL 0x7: rd_dbi_en=1, wr_dbi_en=1, dm_en=1), :4398 (INIT4 emr2=0xf1 = MR3); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:322
dram:dram.ctl.dbi.note: The init also writes MR3 = 0xF1 (INIT4.emr2). In LPDDR4 (GENERIC) MR3 holds PU-CAL, PDDS and the DBI-RD/WR enables, and data masking is set by MR13 OP[5].

dram:dram.ctl.refresh-mode.statement: All-bank refresh every tREFI = 113 x 32 = 3,616 DFI clocks = 3.875 us, each taking tRFCab = 262 DFI clocks = 280.7 ns; per-bank refresh off; temperature derating not enabled.
dram:dram.ctl.refresh-mode.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4441 (RFSHCTL0 0x00210000: per_bank_refresh=0), :4443 (RFSHTMG 0x80710106: t_rfc_nom_x1_x32=0x71, t_rfc_min=0x106), :5475 (RFSHCTL3=0: auto-refresh on after init), :4686-4688 (DERATEEN commented out: 'FUTURE derate is not needed for bring-up'); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/etsoc_hal/inc/DWC_ddr_umctl2.html RFSHTMG.t_rfc_nom_x1_sel ('for ... per-bank refresh only'; unit 'multiples of 32 DFI clock cycles')
dram:dram.ctl.refresh-mode.note: counters-and-dram.md §3.2 had to guess the x32 reading because t_rfc_nom_x1_sel=1; the uMCTL2 register description says x1_sel applies only to per-bank refresh, and the measured period (dram.lat.refresh-period) confirms x32.

dram:dram.ctl.refresh-duty.statement: All-bank refresh keeps each channel busy 280.7 / 3,875 ns = 7.2% of the time; 7.2% of loads issued at random phases landed inside a refresh.

dram:dram.ctl.power-down.statement: No power-down and no self-refresh: the firmware disables both 'for performance reasons', so an idle channel stays in active standby with its clocks running.
dram:dram.ctl.power-down.note: GENERIC consequence: the DRAM's active-standby current flows whenever the card is up; its share of the idle 12-18 W unmetered power is unattributed (hub §4.2).

dram:dram.ctl.zq.statement: Automatic ZQ calibration (the periodic re-trim of the DRAM's output-driver and termination impedance) is disabled.

dram:dram.ctl.dfi-update.statement: The controller requests DFI controller updates (PHY re-trims) automatically every 64-255 x 1,024 DFI clocks (70-280 us).
dram:dram.ctl.dfi-update.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4528-4531 (DFIUPD0 dis_auto_ctrlupd=0; DFIUPD1 interval min 64, max 255 x1024); docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:333
dram:dram.ctl.dfi-update.note: That these cause rare latency blips is an inference (counters-and-dram.md), not measured.

dram:dram.ctl.ports.statement: Each controller has two AXI ports with aging on: port 0 at priority 15 (commented 'lower priority') and port 1 at priority 8 ('higher priority'), for reads and writes alike; the memory shire keeps high/low request lines per controller, and the shire cache marks its to-memory requests high or low QoS from an ESR.
dram:dram.ctl.ports.source: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4670-4680 (PCFGR_0 0x100f, PCFGR_1 0x1008, PCFGW_0 0x100f, PCFGW_1 0x1008); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:95 (`MEMSHIRE_WRITE_CNT_SIZE`, 'one per priority'); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_types.vh (ddrc_esr_ctl_t: u0/u1 csysreq_hi/lo); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.97 §4.1 (esr_sc_axi_qos: AXI_QOS_MEM_HIGH_PRIORITY / _LOW_PRIORITY)
dram:dram.ctl.ports.note: Which traffic is steered to which port, and what esr_sc_axi_qos is set to, is not in the sources (ask).

dram:dram.ctl.cam.statement: The controller's transaction store (CAM) gives 32 entries to low-priority reads (SCHED.lpr_num_entries = 0x1f, 'this value + 1'); the total depth, a build parameter, is not in the sources.

dram:dram.ctl.scheduling.statement: The scheduler serves up to 15 transactions of one kind (high-priority reads, low-priority reads, writes) before switching when another kind waits; low-priority reads and writes may be starved at most 127 clocks, high-priority reads 1.
dram:dram.ctl.scheduling.note: Field meanings are the uMCTL2 register names (xact_run_length, max_starve); the scheduler's algorithm itself is Synopsys's and GENERIC here.

dram:dram.ctl.atomic-unit.statement: The memory shire contains an atomic unit with a small atomic cache (ms_atomic_sm_ctl bits 7:4 flag which entries hold dirty data; a 4-bit state), and the datasheet lists 'LPDDR4X support for global atomic operations'.
dram:dram.ctl.atomic-unit.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.514 Table 15-90 (ms_atomic_sm_ctl); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:121 (`MEMSHIRE_ATOMIC_STATE_SIZE 4`), :268-271 (memshire atomics); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1
dram:dram.ctl.atomic-unit.note: When a global atomic on a DRAM address is done here rather than at the L3 home is not documented (ask).

dram:dram.ctl.registers-sp-only.statement: The memory-shire and DDR-controller registers are reachable only by the service processor.
dram:dram.ctl.registers-sp-only.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf pdf p.512 §15.4.3.1; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:346

dram:dram.ctl.perfmon.statement: Each memory shire has a perf monitor (40-bit cycle counter at 933 MHz and two event counters). The firmware sets them to count mesh reads and writes, which a user kernel can sample through syscall 10; the same monitor can count controller commands (activate, precharge, refresh, per bank), but only M-mode can select that and the encodings are in a document not in the sources.
dram:dram.ctl.perfmon.source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:381-418 (§3.5); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:215-250 (MCOP qualifier: cmd bits 14:0, bank bits 27:20; MESHCNT qualifier)
dram:dram.ctl.perfmon.note: Hub rungs 13-14 and the missing 'Memory Shire Specification §5.4.22-29'.

dram:dram.lat.typical.statement: A typical DRAM load, timed one at a time: 299 cycles (500 ns at 600 MHz), the median of 4,500 loads from shire 0 to random lines; 299 in each of 15 passes on three cards.
dram:dram.lat.typical.source: docs/reports/2026-09-19-et-soc1-memory-anatomy.html headline tile 'A DRAM load, typical' (19 Sep: 4,500 loads; 26 Sep: 15 passes on three cards)

dram:dram.lat.chase.statement: A DRAM pointer chase: 296.6-297.1 cycles from shires 0 and 31, 287.2-288.8 from shires 7 and 24 (479-495 ns at 600 MHz), in every pass on every card.
dram:dram.lat.chase.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/lat.json items[LAT-M2].per_card.<card>.passes[].DRAM; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'L3 and DRAM latency by requesting shire' (E36)
dram:dram.lat.chase.note: About 490 ns, a fifth more than an A100's HBM (405 ns).

dram:dram.lat.clock-scaling.statement: At 800 MHz the chase reads 352-368 cycles (440-460 ns): the mesh and DDR parts do not scale with the minion clock; fitted, a DRAM load is 86.3 minion cycles + 344.8 ns.

dram:dram.lat.model.statement: Whole DRAM load = 110 + 12 x hops(requester -> L3 home) + 91 + 12 x hops(L3 home -> memory shire) cycles; left as fitted on aifoundry2, within +-3 cycles for 97.0% of lines on aifoundry2, 92.9% on aifoundry3, 94.4% on aifoundry1-c1.
dram:dram.lat.model.source: anatomy page §4 (formula); docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM latency against the 19 September model' (E35, docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P2)
dram:dram.lat.model.note: Refitted pass by pass the constant reads 90-91 on all three cards (docs/reports/data/2026-09-26-memprobe-3cards/cards.json ms_const).

dram:dram.lat.ms-hops.statement: With the memory shires one hop outside the grid, the memory shire's position adds 12-84 cycles (1-7 hops from the L3 home, 2.6 on average).

dram:dram.lat.dram-chip-share.statement: Of the 91-cycle constant (152 ns), about 28 cycles are the DRAM's own timing: the activate (tRCD, 11 cycles) and the read latency plus two 32-byte bursts (19.3 + 8.6 ns, 17 cycles). The rest, at most about 63 cycles (~105 ns), is the L3 home's miss path and its To_Sys crossings (about 12 cycles by the spec: an L3 miss is 42 shire clocks against 30 for a hit) plus the memory shire's port, clock crossing, controller and PHY.
dram:dram.lat.dram-chip-share.source: anatomy page §4 ('Of the 91 cycles (152 ns), the DRAM chip itself accounts for about 28'); dram.ctl.tRCD, dram.ctl.RL-WL, dram.ctl.burst; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.11 Table 1 ('L3 cache read hit 30', 'L3 cache read miss 42 + NoC & Mem latency')
dram:dram.lat.dram-chip-share.note: The 91 is a DRAM load minus an L3 hit at the same home (dram.lat.model), so it includes the home's extra work on a miss, not only the memory shire. 'At most' because each hop further out that the memory shires might sit moves 12 cycles from the constant into the mesh legs.

dram:dram.lat.ms-internal.statement: How the ~63 cycles beyond the DRAM's own timing split between the L3 home's miss handling and To_Sys crossings, the memory shire's NoC AXI port and clock crossing, the address strip, the controller's port, CAM and scheduler, the DFI and the PHY's transmit and receive paths is not known.
dram:dram.lat.ms-internal.source: none: no memory-shire description is in the sources (hub ask 'ask-memshire', docs/reports/sources/limits-of-observability.data.json improvements[25])

dram:dram.lat.row-hit.statement: A load that finds its row open skips the activate and saves 11-12 cycles (about 19 ns, tRCD): 214 against 226 cycles in the refresh series; the two clusters' means were 11.0-11.6 cycles apart on three cards.
dram:dram.lat.row-hit.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json refresh.open_med = 214, refresh.closed_med = 226, refresh.closed_minus_open = 11.6; anatomy page §5 #refresh-caught-in-the-act; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM refresh and open rows' (E35)
dram:dram.lat.row-hit.note: The registered three-card test read 5.3-6.6 cycles because it missed the later build's 7-cycle timer offset; re-referenced to each pass's own L1 hit it reads 11.0-11.6 (anatomy page, 'Checked on three cards').

dram:dram.lat.row-conflict.statement: Two loads to the same bank but different rows, issued together: the second pays about +37 cycles (36.9 on aifoundry2, 37.4 on aifoundry3, 36.5 on aifoundry1-c1; 38.5 on 19 September): it cannot activate its row until tRC (63.2 ns = 37.9 cycles) after the first activate.
dram:dram.lat.row-conflict.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json [item=MEM-P4].per_card.<card>.tests.P4_row_conflict_extra; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM bank timing (bits)' (E35); anatomy page §5
dram:dram.lat.row-conflict.note: The tRC explanation is et-derived: the penalty matches the programmed tRC within a cycle.

dram:dram.lat.row-sequential.statement: Issued one after the other: a second load to another row of the same bank pays about +9-10 cycles (the precharge, tRP = 11 cycles), one to the same row saves 11-12, one to another bank costs nothing extra.
dram:dram.lat.row-sequential.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json bits['18'..'29'].b_minus_b0_med = 9, bits['13'..'17'] = -12; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json MEM-P4 P4_seq_row, P4_seq_col, P4_seq_bank (+10, -11, 0 on every card)

dram:dram.lat.rows-closed.statement: Every load of the latency decomposition found its row closed: each came 2,600 cycles or more after its row was last opened, longer than a refresh period; after up to 27 ms idle a DRAM load is 10.5 cycles slower, the row closure, and no other wake-up cost.
dram:dram.lat.rows-closed.source: anatomy page §4 ('Every one of these loads found its row closed'); docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'No array wake-up latency' (E18)

dram:dram.lat.refresh-period.statement: Folding 19,000 DRAM load times on their timestamps shows refresh every 2,325.4 cycles = 3.876 us on every card (15 passes); a load that arrives during a refresh waits up to 208 extra cycles (347 ns), and refresh closes the open row.
dram:dram.lat.refresh-period.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json refresh.period_cycles = 2325.4, refresh.max_wait = 208; docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/mem.json [item=MEM-P5].per_card.<card>.tests.P5_refresh_period, .P5_max_extra; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM refresh and open rows' (E35)
dram:dram.lat.refresh-period.note: Matches the programmed tREFI (3.875 us) to 0.02%. The 208-cycle wait is 347 ns against tRFCab 280.7 ns; the remaining ~66 ns is not attributed (a precharge-all before the refresh and the re-activate after it are the GENERIC candidates).

dram:dram.lat.row-life.statement: A row stays open until a refresh or a conflicting load closes it; no idle timer was seen: in the refresh series 96% of loads with no refresh since the previous one were row hits (3,556 of 3,713, after 450-2,000 idle cycles), 4% across a refresh.
dram:dram.lat.row-life.unit: % row hits without a refresh between

dram:dram.lat.l3-miss.statement: The DRAM leg starts when the L3 home's cache bank misses: the L3 miss costs 42 shire clocks (idle, excluding NoC and memory) and the bank sends the read through its 512-bit To_Sys port into the NoC.
dram:dram.lat.l3-miss.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.11 Table 1 ('L3 cache read miss 42 + NoC & Mem latency'), pdf p.8 ('it uses its 512b To_Sys port into the NoC to make the request to the memory'), pdf p.55 (misses and victims to the to_sys port)

dram:dram.e.per-byte.statement: Reading DRAM costs 114.6 pJ per byte above idle [89.0-141.3 over 18 passes] with 1 KB tensor loads at 600 MHz (aifoundry2 111.5, aifoundry3 105.6, aifoundry1-c1 126.6): about 7.3 nJ per 64-byte line.
dram:dram.e.per-byte.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json reruns.levels_pj_per_byte['dram'] (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table row 'DRAM'

dram:dram.e.data.statement: Even DRAM is data-dependent: a tensor load from DRAM costs 94.6 pJ/B on zeros [86.2-105.7] and 132.6 on random data [117.9-145.4]; a tensor store 94.4 and 141.9.
dram:dram.e.data.note: With read and write DBI on and LVSTL I/O terminated to ground (GENERIC), driving ones costs current and zeros almost none; that is one plausible share of the gap, not measured separately.

dram:dram.e.writeback.statement: Stores to DRAM through the L1 write-back path (fsw.ps) cost 341.5 pJ/B on random data at 27 GB/s: each store allocates its line, so the byte pays a DRAM read and a DRAM write.
dram:dram.e.writeback.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.combined['st_stream/dram/random']; docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table row 'fsw.ps stores to DRAM through the L1'

dram:dram.e.store-vs-load.statement: A tensor store to DRAM is not distinguishable from a tensor load in energy on any card (+8.4, +7.3 and +14.5 pJ/B, 99% intervals all including 0).
dram:dram.e.store-vs-load.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/cat.json [item=CAT-e].per_card.<card>.tstore_minus_tload; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'A tensor store to DRAM against a tensor load, random' (E45)

dram:dram.e.unmetered.statement: About 70% of a DRAM byte's energy lands on no metered rail: a DRAM tensor load splits 2% minion cores, 11% SRAM, 18% mesh, 69% unmetered; the fit of the unmetered remainder puts 72.7 (aifoundry2), 72.7 (aifoundry3) and 81.6 (aifoundry1-c1) pJ per DRAM byte in the DDR PHY, the I/O rail and the DRAM chips.
dram:dram.e.unmetered.source: docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md rail-split table row 'DRAM, tensor load' and unmetered-fit table row 'per DRAM byte'; docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json unmetered.<card>.coef.dram_pj_per_byte; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'Rail split, DRAM read'

dram:dram.e.split-unknown.statement: How the ~73 pJ/B off-rail DRAM energy splits between the memory shires' logic, the PHY's I/O, the DRAM core (activate, sensing, column path) and the DRAM's own I/O is not measurable on the card: none of those rails has a current sensor.
dram:dram.e.split-unknown.source: docs/findings/19-observability-and-the-unmetered.md ('The other rails — DDR core 0.8 V, VDDQ 1.1 V, VDDQLP ... have set points in the PMIC and no telemetry'); docs/research/power-telemetry.md:47-52, 255

dram:dram.e.rows.statement: The DRAM row pattern does not change the energy per byte: row hits 155.9, row misses 158.5, sequential 156.4 pJ/B on random data (120.4 / 118.5 / 120.6 on zeros), indistinguishable on every card; an activation costing 30 pJ/B on zeros or 50 on random data would have shown.
dram:dram.e.rows.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/manual.json catalogue.combined['dramrow2/rowhit/random'], ['dramrow2/rowmiss/random'], ['dramrow2/seq/random'] (and /zeros); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md '## Rows: does the DRAM row pattern matter?'; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DRAM row walks (seq, rowhit, rowmiss) over a DRAM tensor load' (E45)
dram:dram.e.rows.note: The manual's caveat: with 32 streams interleaved and a refresh every 2,325 cycles, every pattern may have paid an activation; so the activate energy is bounded, not measured. Per 64-byte line the bound is ~1.9 nJ (zeros) to ~3.2 nJ (random).

dram:dram.e.gather.statement: A random 4-byte element gathered from DRAM costs 9.8 nJ (a whole line fetched for 4 bytes), at 1.19 G elements/s chip-wide; a scatter into DRAM 23.8 nJ at 0.42 G/s.
dram:dram.e.gather.source: docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md table rows 'DRAM' (gathers and scatters); docs/reports/data/2026-09-25-claims-v3/results/gs.json items['GS-RATE'].pooled

dram:dram.e.vs-scp.statement: On random data DRAM is 30x the energy of the shire's own scratchpad per byte read (132.6 against 4.40 pJ/B) and 17x per byte written; relaying a result through DRAM costs 12.9-13.1x handing it to the next shire.
dram:dram.e.vs-scp.source: docs/energy-manual/04-bytes-memory.md:37 ('DRAM is 30x the energy ...'), the random-data rows of its tables; docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'The relay (V3)' (E29)
dram:dram.e.vs-scp.page: Hand it to the next shire

dram:dram.pwr.rails.statement: Three card rails serve the memory path: VDD_DDR (the memory shires, 0.8 V set point, 875 mV in the card's power-tree figure), VDD_QLP (the LPDDR4X I/O VDDQ; 640 mV set point read on aifoundry2, 620 mV in the figure) and VDD_Q (1.1 V: the LPDDR4X's VDDQ/VDD2 core supply, as the figure labels it). None reports current.
dram:dram.pwr.rails.source: docs/research/power-telemetry.md:47-52 (from the power-tree images, external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf pdf pp.2-4); docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace2-telemetry.jsonl fields reg_mv.ddr = 800, reg_mv.vddqlp = 640, reg_mv.vddq = 1100
dram:dram.pwr.rails.note: JEDEC LPDDR4X (GENERIC): VDD1 1.8 V, VDD2 1.1 V, VDDQ 0.6 V. Which card rail feeds the DRAM's VDD1 is not in the sources.

dram:dram.pwr.droop.statement: The memory shires' own voltage monitors read the 0.8 V DDR rail at 767-768 mV at idle, and it droops 0.86-1.01 mV per watt of off-rail DRAM power (1 mV ~ 1.2 W of DRAM): a proxy DRAM meter, refreshed every service-processor pass.
dram:dram.pwr.droop.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md, row 'DDR rail droop per off-rail DRAM watt' (E30, E46); docs/energy-manual/04a-fine-grain.md 'A droop meter for DRAM'; horace2-telemetry.jsonl die_mv.ddr

dram:gen.cell.statement: A DRAM bit is one 1T1C cell: an NMOS access transistor whose gate is the wordline and whose drain is the bitline, in series with a storage capacitor; the stored charge is the bit, it leaks away (hence refresh), and reading it is destructive until the sense amplifier restores it.
dram:gen.cell.source: GENERIC (textbook DRAM; no ET source describes the die)

dram:gen.equalize.statement: Between accesses each bitline pair is held at half the array voltage by a precharge/equalize circuit (typically three NMOS: two tie BL and /BL to the half-voltage, one shorts them together); the equalize signal turns off just before a wordline rises.

dram:gen.wordline.statement: Activate: the row address is decoded, and the selected (sub-)wordline driver pulls its wordline up to a boosted voltage above the array voltage, so every access NMOS on that row turns fully on and passes a full level.

dram:gen.sense.statement: Each cell shares its charge with its bitline, nudging it slightly above or below the half-voltage; the bitline sense amplifier, a cross-coupled latch of two NMOS and two PMOS, is then fired (NMOS side pulled to ground, PMOS side to the array voltage) and drives the pair to full rail, which also rewrites the cell. The row of latched sense amplifiers is the open page ('row buffer').
dram:gen.sense.note: On the ET-SoC-1's channels one activate latches 16,384 bits (dram.org.geometry).

dram:gen.column.statement: Read: the column decoder raises a column-select line, turning on column-select NMOS pairs that connect the chosen sense amplifiers to local and then global I/O lines, where secondary sense amplifiers pick up the data; LPDDR4 fetches 16 bits per DQ per READ (16n prefetch), 256 bits for a x16 channel, and serialises them 16:1 onto each pin.
dram:gen.column.source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 LPDDR4 16n prefetch; array circuit textbook)

dram:gen.io.statement: LPDDR4X signals use LVSTL: each DQ driver pulls up to a 0.6 V VDDQ or down to ground, and the receiver terminates to ground, so a driven 1 draws current through the termination and a 0 almost none; DBI inverts a byte that holds more than four ones. (LPDDR4's LVSTL pull-up is usually an NMOS, N-over-N; the transistor choice is the vendor's.)
dram:gen.io.note: ET has read and write DBI on (dram.ctl.dbi); the card's VDD_QLP set point is 620-640 mV (dram.pwr.rails).

dram:gen.precharge.statement: Precharge: the wordline falls (access transistors off, the restored cells isolated), the sense amplifiers are disabled and the equalizers turn back on, returning every bitline pair to the half-voltage for the next activate.

dram:gen.commands.statement: LPDDR4 commands travel on a 6-bit single-data-rate command/address bus: an ACTIVATE is two 2-clock parts (ACT-1, ACT-2), a READ or WRITE is RD-1/WR-1 plus CAS-2 (4 clocks), a PRECHARGE 2 clocks.

dram:gen.refresh.statement: All-bank refresh: the die's internal counter supplies the row addresses and each REFab activates and precharges a batch of rows in every bank at once; JEDEC LPDDR4 asks for 8,192 refresh commands per 32 ms retention window at normal temperature, which with 131,072 rows per bank means 16 rows of each bank per REFab.
dram:gen.refresh.source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 tREFW 32 ms, 8,192 REF); rows per bank from dram.org.geometry
dram:gen.refresh.note: ET's tREFI 3.875 us is slightly shorter than JEDEC's 3.904 us, so 8,192 refreshes take 31.7 ms.

dram:gen.temp-refresh.statement: LPDDR4 needs refresh 2x or 4x as often above 85 C, signalled in its MR4 register. The ET firmware leaves derating off, so refresh stays at 3.875 us whatever the DRAM temperature; nothing in the sources reads the DRAM's temperature.
dram:gen.temp-refresh.source: GENERIC (JEDEC JESD209-4 MR4 refresh-rate field); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4686-4688 (DERATEEN commented out)
dram:gen.temp-refresh.note: Whether the packages stay under 85 C under load is an ask; the die itself idles at 72 C and reaches 80-90 C under load on these cards.

dram:gen.jedec-match.statement: The programmed timings are close to JEDEC LPDDR4's limits for a 16 Gb-per-channel die at 3,733 MT/s, as recalled from JESD209-4 and not checked against the standard: tRCD and tRPpb 18 ns minimum, tRAS 42 ns, tRRD 10 ns, tFAW 40 ns, tRFCab 280 ns; RL 36 (with read DBI) and WL 16 are the fixed read and write latencies for this rate, and tREFI 3.875 us is just under the 3.904 us maximum interval.
dram:gen.jedec-match.source: GENERIC comparison: JEDEC JESD209-4 values recalled, not checked against the standard (no ET source); ET values from dram.ctl.*
dram:gen.jedec-match.note: tRFCab = 280 ns is the JEDEC value for 12-16 Gb per channel, a cross-check on the die density.

dram:dram.store.path.statement: A store reaches DRAM only when its dirty line leaves the L3: the L3 bank sends the victim as a write through its To_Sys port to the memory shire PA[8:6] names; the controller queues it in its write store and drains writes in runs of up to 15.
dram:dram.store.path.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.8 (L3 evicts via To_Sys), p.55 (misses and victims to the to_sys port), pp.79-83 (Flush/FlushToMem); external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4667 (PERFWR1)

dram:dram.refill.path.statement: The line comes back the way the request went: the memory shire answers the L3 home over the mesh, the L3 installs it and returns it to the requester; the latency model counts 12 cycles per hop on both legs.
dram:dram.refill.path.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.54-55 (misses to to_sys; data returned and installed), p.8; anatomy page §4 (model)

dram:dram.seq.load.01.statement: The L3 home misses and sends a 64-byte read with its QoS over the 512-bit To_Sys port.

dram:dram.seq.load.02.statement: The request crosses 1-7 mesh hops to the memory shire that PA[8:6] names.
dram:dram.seq.load.02.value: 12 cycles per hop, round trip (both directions counted here)

dram:dram.seq.load.03.statement: The memory shire accepts the read, crosses from the mesh clock into its own domain, uses PA[9] to pick controller u0 or u1 (the channel) and strips PA[9:6] from the address.
dram:dram.seq.load.03.value: part of the memory shire's <=63 cycles; split unknown
dram:dram.seq.load.03.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf pdf p.30 §7.1.1.1; external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/include/hwinc/ms_regs.h:160 (ms_mem_ctl reset); external/core-et/rtl/inc/memshire_defines.vh:21-22; clock crossing: anatomy page §4 ('the crossings between the 933 MHz DDR clock and the mesh')
dram:dram.seq.load.03.note: Where inside the memory shire the clock crossing sits, and whether its logic runs at 933 MHz, is inferred, not documented.

dram:dram.seq.load.04.statement: The controller maps the address to bank PA[12:10], row PA[34:18], columns PA[17:13] and PA[5:1], queues the read and finds the bank closed (open-page policy, but the last refresh closed it).
dram:dram.seq.load.04.value: part of the memory shire's <=63 cycles

dram:dram.seq.load.05.statement: The controller issues ACTIVATE (ACT-1, ACT-2) with bank and row; the PHY drives it onto the channel's CA pins at 1,866 MHz.
dram:dram.seq.load.05.value: 4 DRAM clocks on the bus (2.1 ns)

dram:dram.seq.load.06.statement: The bank's equalizers let go of the bitlines and the selected wordline rises to its boosted level: 16,384 access transistors (one 2 KB page) turn on.

dram:dram.seq.load.07.statement: The sense amplifiers fire and latch the whole row, restoring every cell; the bank is open once tRCD has passed.
dram:dram.seq.load.07.value: tRCD 18.2 ns = 11 cycles (measured: a row hit saves 11-12)

dram:dram.seq.load.08.statement: Two READs (RD-1 + CAS-2 each) fetch the line's two 32-byte halves from the open row: same columns PA[17:13], PA[5] = 0 then 1.
dram:dram.seq.load.08.value: tCCD 4.3 ns between the two READs

dram:dram.seq.load.09.statement: After the read latency the DRAM drives two BL16 bursts, 32 bytes each, at 3,733 MT/s with read DBI; the PHY's trained receivers capture them on the strobe.
dram:dram.seq.load.09.value: RL 19.3 ns + 2 x 4.3 ns bursts = 17 cycles

dram:dram.seq.load.10.statement: The line goes back through the controller and the memory shire's clock crossing onto the 512-bit NoC port. The row stays open: no precharge follows (open page, no auto-precharge).
dram:dram.seq.load.10.value: rest of the memory shire's <=63 cycles; the whole memory-shire leg is 91 cycles + 12 per hop

dram:dram.seq.load.11.statement: The response returns to the L3 home, which installs the line and forwards it to the requesting shire.
dram:dram.seq.load.11.value: whole load ~297-299 cycles (~490-500 ns); DRAM chip ~28 of them

dram:dram.seq.row-hit.01.statement: If the row is still open (no refresh and no other row of the bank since), the controller skips steps 5-7 and issues the READs at once.
dram:dram.seq.row-hit.01.value: -11 to -12 cycles against a closed row

dram:dram.seq.row-conflict.01.statement: If another row of the bank is open, the controller first precharges it, then activates the new row; an ACT to the same bank cannot follow the previous ACT sooner than tRC.
dram:dram.seq.row-conflict.01.value: +9-10 cycles issued after (tRP), +37 cycles issued together (tRC 63.2 ns)

dram:dram.seq.store.01.statement: A dirty line leaves the L3 (eviction, flush to memory, or a tensor store that bypasses the caches) as a 64-byte write to the memory shire PA[8:6] names.
dram:dram.seq.store.01.note: A store through the L1 (fsw.ps) first reads its line from DRAM: that byte pays a read and a write.

dram:dram.seq.store.02.statement: The write is queued with its data; the scheduler drains writes in runs of up to 15 and pays read/write turnarounds.

dram:dram.seq.store.03.statement: WRITE (WR-1 + CAS-2); 16 DRAM clocks later the PHY drives 32 bytes on DQ with write DBI and data mask available.

dram:dram.seq.store.04.statement: The DRAM's write drivers overpower the selected sense amplifiers through the column-select transistors; the latches flip and, through the still-open access transistors, charge or discharge the cell capacitors.
dram:dram.seq.store.04.value: write recovery nWR 34 DRAM clocks (18.2 ns) before any precharge

dram:dram.seq.store.05.statement: Tensor stores to DRAM run at 76 GB/s and cost 94.4 pJ/B on zeros, 141.9 on random data, indistinguishable from tensor loads; stores through the L1 cost 341.5 pJ/B at 27 GB/s.

dram:dram.seq.refresh.01.statement: Every tREFI (3,616 DFI clocks = 3.875 us) the controller closes the channel's open rows and issues an all-bank REFRESH; no per-bank refresh and no temperature derating.
dram:dram.seq.refresh.01.value: measured period 2,325.4 cycles = 3.876 us on every card

dram:dram.seq.refresh.02.statement: The die activates and precharges a batch of rows in every bank (about 16 per bank per REFab for this density), with no column access: the same wordline, charge-sharing, sense and restore, and precharge switching as an activate, times the batch.

dram:dram.seq.refresh.03.statement: A load that meets the refresh waits up to 208 cycles (347 ns); 7.2% of random-phase loads do; the next load after it finds its row closed and pays an activate (+11-12 cycles).

dram:dram.seq.refresh.04.statement: Refresh energy is part of the idle power, which the card's meters do not split; it is not measured.

dram:dram.u-ports.statement: Which traffic the memory shire steers to each controller's two AXI ports (priority 15 and 8).
dram:dram.u-ports.source: none: dram.ctl.ports gives the ports' priorities (memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4670-4680), not the steering

dram:dram.u-qos.statement: What esr_sc_axi_qos is set to on these cards, so whether the shire cache marks its memory requests high or low priority.
dram:dram.u-qos.source: none: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf pdf p.97 §4.1 defines the field; no value is read or written in the sources

dram:dram.u-atomic.statement: When a global atomic on a DRAM address is done in the memory shire's atomic unit rather than at the L3 home.
dram:dram.u-atomic.source: none: dram.ctl.atomic-unit documents the unit (PRM pdf p.514; memshire_defines.vh:121), not when it is used

dram:dram.u-cam.statement: The controller's total transaction-store (CAM) depth, MEMC_NO_OF_ENTRY, a build parameter; the init code sets only the 32 entries for low-priority reads.

dram:dram.u-ms-clock.statement: Where inside the memory shire the mesh-to-controller clock crossing sits, and whether the memory shire's logic runs at the 933 MHz DFI clock.
dram:dram.u-ms-clock.source: none: dram.seq.load.03 infers it from the anatomy page's 'crossings between the 933 MHz DDR clock and the mesh'

dram:dram.u-temp.statement: Whether the DRAM packages stay under 85 C under load. The firmware leaves temperature derating off, so refresh stays at 3.875 us whatever their temperature; above 85 C LPDDR4 asks for refresh 2x or 4x as often (GENERIC), so this is a data-retention question, not only a performance one.
dram:dram.u-temp.source: none: external/et-platform/etsoc-hal/src/memshire_ddr_init_functions.c:4686-4688 (DERATEEN commented out); nothing in the sources reads MR4

dram:dram.u-vdd1.statement: Which card rail feeds the LPDDR4X packages' VDD1 (1.8 V in JEDEC LPDDR4X, GENERIC).
dram:dram.u-vdd1.source: none: the card's power tree (docs/research/power-telemetry.md:47-52) names VDD_DDR, VDD_QLP and VDD_Q only

chip:mesh.logical-map.statement: Measured position of each compute shire on the 6 × 6 grid (marty1885's logical map, x across, y down): y=0: 0 24 9 25 2 11; y=1: 8 16 1 17 10 19; y=2: 3 4 13 14 18 27; y=3: _ 12 21 22 26 _; y=4: _ 20 29 30 15 23; y=5: _ 28 5 6 7 31.
chip:mesh.logical-map.source: workloads/nocbench/analyze.py:52-60 (`MARTY`, `EMPTY`); docs/findings/05-claims.md:383, 412 (map recovered from latency alone in 12 of 12 search restarts on every card)
chip:mesh.logical-map.note: Built by marty1885's etTopoScan from bandwidth on another card; confirmed by TensorSend latency on all three lab cards. Shire IDs are the firmware's logical IDs.

chip:mesh.grid.statement: The NoC is an 8 × 6 grid of mesh stops: 34 minion shires, 1 PCIe shire, 1 I/O shire and 8 memory shires; the four memory shires on each side leave the grid's corners empty, so there are 44 mesh stops.
chip:mesh.grid.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.21 (§4 ET-SoC-1 Mesh Network on Chip)

chip:L40.statement: Fitting DRAM latency with one shared constant plus 12 cycles per hop, and each memory shire one hop outside the grid, puts memory shires 0–3 above the grid and 4–7 below it at x = 1…4 (logical frame): MS0 (1,-1), MS1 (2,-1), MS2 (3,-1), MS3 (4,-1), MS4 (1,6), MS5 (2,6), MS6 (3,6), MS7 (4,6); total squared error 2 cycles² over 32 home/memory-shire pairs.
chip:L40.note: The fit tried only positions one hop outside the grid; moving all eight one hop further out fits equally with a constant of 79.

chip:L42.statement: Memory shire 2's position is a tie-break: its four home shires all sit in column x = 4, so x = 3 or x = 5 above the grid, or (6, 0) beside it, fit equally.

chip:L105.statement: Each mesh stop has 9 main-NoC routers (layers 0–8) plus one debug-NoC router; routers have 8 ports (H, E, S, W, N, I, J, K) with 4 VC slots each; route info, packet, sideband and data are parity-protected (no ECC).
chip:L105.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1b rows 'Main-NoC layers', 'Router ports and VCs', 'Error protection' (etsoc_shire_other_esr.h:3877-3981; noc_esr.h)
chip:L105.note: SYNTHESIS marks these 'U' (not independently re-verified); router-to-router flit width is unknown.

chip:L104.statement: The mesh routes in dimension order, and a request and its reply take opposite orders: a request goes x first, then y, and a reply y first, then x, on the logical map, so a reply retraces its request's route backwards. Measured on 29 September (E56) with sets of streams between shires chosen so that their streams share one directed link under one order and none under the other: 1 KB tensor loads, whose data travel as replies, fell to 0.54-0.77 of their bandwidth alone when they shared a link under y first and held at 1.00 when they shared one under x first; tensor stores, whose data travel as requests, showed the mirror (0.52-0.76 against 1.00). A shared link carried about 92 GB/s. The same on aifoundry1 card 1 (development), aifoundry3 (the frozen validation) and aifoundry2 (the same frozen test, run as a third card on the evening of 29 September), three passes each.
chip:L104.source: tools/claims-v3/nocr/PREREG.md (frozen 29 Sep about 00:10 PDT, sha256 2472ab3e...; the sets: workloads/nocroute/meshmap.py, tools/claims-v3/nocr/sets.json); docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-nocr/raw/<card>/summary.json .r32.read and .r32.write: .verdict, .sets.<set>.rho_pooled (sets of 3 and 5 streams), .capacity_gbs_from_dropping_sets; docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-nocr/README.md
chip:L104.note: Until 29 September this fact was inferred: the analyses assumed x first for every packet (as Chang infers), and every route on this page was drawn so (docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1b 'Routing'; heat-per-mm.script.js's route map, x first by default until 29 September: its `order` and the 'Routing order' toggle). What E56 saw is the data: a load's replies and a store's requests. That a load's own requests go x first and a store's acknowledgements y first follows if the order is set by the kind of packet; those small packets never slowed a set (each costs a link under 0.54 of a reply). On the die view x runs down the die's rows: a request first moves north or south, then east or west, and a reply first east or west.

scp:scp.seq.own-load.01.statement: minion: tensor-load unit (DCache TensorLoad 0 FSM): Hart 0 writes CSR 0x83F; the FSM expands it into up to 16 line reads (address + i x stride), keeping up to 4 in flight. A scalar or vector load instead misses the L1 and a miss handler (2 per minion) asks for the line.
scp:scp.seq.own-load.01.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.275; external/core-et/docs/Minion DCache Description.pdf p.40-44; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:448-449
scp:scp.seq.own-load.01.note: Time: about 10 cycles per extra line with 4 in flight (measured)

scp:scp.seq.own-load.02.statement: address decode: Bits [39:31] = 9'h1 mark the scratchpad; the shire field (0x7F or the own ID) makes it local; bank = PA[7:6].
scp:scp.seq.own-load.02.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf p.24; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.486

scp:scp.seq.own-load.03.statement: neighbourhood request path: The minion's 256-bit ET-Link request enters the neighbourhood arbiter and a 3-deep bank FIFO, crosses from the low-voltage minion region into the high-voltage region on the shire clock, and is up-converted onto the neighbourhood's one 512-bit ET-Link.
scp:scp.seq.own-load.03.note: Time: at least 6 clocks for a minion (4 for other agents)

scp:scp.seq.own-load.04.statement: request crossbar: Per-neighbourhood catch FIFO at the target bank; a round-robin arbiter picks one source per bank per cycle.

scp:scp.seq.own-load.05.statement: bank reqq (64 entries): Allocate an entry (stages ag, ad); compare with the read buffer (a hit goes to the RBUF: 10 shire clocks, 36 minion cycles load-to-use); check the index against the scratchpad region (error if beyond 640 sets); per sub-bank, round-robin among neighbourhood requests, L3-slave requests first, masked by sub-bank busy (stage rqa).

scp:scp.seq.own-load.06.statement: tag pipeline stages (tap, ta, ta0, ta1, te, tc): For a scratchpad address the tag and tag-state RAM reads are squashed: nothing is compared, the request is a hit by definition, way = PA[11:10], set = PA[21:12]. The stages still elapse, which is why the scratchpad is exactly as fast as an L2 hit.
scp:scp.seq.own-load.06.note: Time: fixed stages (part of the 21 shire clocks); Energy: tag and tag-state panels idle

scp:scp.seq.own-load.07.statement: data panels of sub-bank PA[9:8] (four 4,096 x 144 macros, one per quadword): Stages dap, da, da0, da1: the panel clock is gated on; row {set, way} = PA[21:10] is read in all four panels at once; 576 bits (512 data + 64 ECC) come out after the 2-cycle access.
scp:scp.seq.own-load.07.note: Time: 2 shire-cache cycles (3.3 ns if at 600 MHz); Energy: about 182 pJ per line on the SRAM rail with random data, 92 with zeros (aifoundry2)

scp:scp.seq.own-load.08.statement: ECC check (stage de): SECDED over 8 x (64 + 8) bits: a single-bit error is corrected, a double reported; no scrubbing on this chip.

scp:scp.seq.own-load.09.statement: data complete (stage dc), read buffer, response mux: The line is OR'ed out of the sub-bank, installed in the 8-entry read buffer (esr_sc_scp_rbuf_enable) and sent to the response mux's per-neighbourhood FIFO, or parked in the dataq if the mux is busy.

scp:scp.seq.own-load.10.statement: response crossbar and neighbourhood fill path: The 512-bit line crosses the response crossbar into the neighbourhood's 4-entry Fill FIFO (one response per cycle, one every other cycle per agent), back into the minion region, and down the minion's 256-bit port in two beats.
scp:scp.seq.own-load.10.note: Time: Fill FIFO at least 2 clocks; minion response path at least 2; 6 in all for a minion; Energy: the whole fill of a line into the L1: 101 pJ zeros, 238 pJ random (measured)

scp:scp.seq.own-load.11.statement: L1 scratchpad (latch RAM) or TenB buffer: The TensorLoad FSM writes the line into consecutive L1-scratchpad lines (latch RAM, 4 blocks of 128 x 64 b); TensorLoad Setup B puts it in the VPU's 4-entry buffer instead; an ordinary load fills an L1 line.

scp:scp.seq.own-store.01.statement: minion: TensorStore (CSR 0x87F): Reads rows of 16, 32, 48 or 64 B from the vector registers and sends them as ET-Link writes (256-bit datapath; a 64 B row is a two-beat transfer), bypassing the L1 and L2 caches.
scp:scp.seq.own-store.01.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.306; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf p.15-20

scp:scp.seq.own-store.02.statement: neighbourhood, request crossbar, bank reqq and dataq: As a load, but the data rides along and waits in the dataq entry; a local scratchpad write-around is turned into a regular write before the shire cache.

scp:scp.seq.own-store.03.statement: pipeline: Tag and tag-state reads squashed; writes of 16 B or more are full-quadword writes (no read-modify-write); any read-buffer copy of the line is cleared.

scp:scp.seq.own-store.04.statement: data panels (only the written quadwords' panels are clocked): Per-quadword write enable: a 32 B row writes 2 of the 4 panels, a 64 B row all 4.
scp:scp.seq.own-store.04.note: Time: 2 cycles; Energy: about 2.1x a read per byte on the SRAM rail

scp:scp.seq.own-store.05.statement: acknowledgement: REP_Ack back through the response crossbar; TensorWait retires the store.
scp:scp.seq.own-store.05.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf p.12 Table 2 (REQ_Write local SCP), p.58-59 §3.4; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.25 (TensorWait), p.272-274 §9.3

scp:scp.seq.remote-load.01.statement: requesting minion, neighbourhood, request crossbar, bank: The shire field does not match: the reqq sends a Mesh_Read instead of using the pipeline.

scp:scp.seq.remote-load.02.statement: to_l3 mesh master (4 ports): Request xbar onto one of 4 ports, ET-Link converted to AXI AR, through a voltage-and-clock-crossing FIFO into the mesh.
scp:scp.seq.remote-load.02.note: Time: part of the ~53 cycles of leaving and entering shires

scp:scp.seq.remote-load.03.statement: mesh (NoC routers and links, 0.485 V, 400 MHz): The request and later the 64 B response cross the mesh: 12 minion cycles (20 ns, 8 mesh cycles) per hop, round trip.
scp:scp.seq.remote-load.03.note: Time: 12.00 cycles per hop (measured); Energy: 0.67 / 1.80 pJ/B per hop (zeros / random, board); mesh rail 1.27 pJ/B per hop

scp:scp.seq.remote-load.04.statement: target shire: mesh slave (L3-slave port, 4 ports) and bank L3 slave: AXI to ET-Link, onto the bank's L3-slave FIFO; up to 21 reqq entries are reserved for such requests and they beat local neighbourhood requests in each sub-bank's arbitration.

scp:scp.seq.remote-load.05.statement: target bank: read buffer or pipeline and data panels: Exactly steps 6-9 of the local load (tags squashed, 4 panels read, ECC); an L3-slave scratchpad read may also hit and fill the read buffer.
scp:scp.seq.remote-load.05.note: Time: the pipeline; Energy: rail split at 1 hop: 50% SRAM, 27% mesh, 14% minions

scp:scp.seq.remote-load.06.statement: return: rspmux_l3, mesh, requester's to_l3 port, bank response FIFO, response crossbar, neighbourhood: AXI R data back over the mesh to the requesting bank, which forwards it to the neighbourhood as for a local load.

scp:scp.seq.remote-store.01.statement: local bank: A plain remote write goes from the dataq straight to the mesh; a TensorStore write-around is coalesced in the local L2 (a partial line occupies a local L2 line and the coalescing buffer) and sent when all four quadwords are present; a full-line write-around that misses bypasses the local panels.
scp:scp.seq.remote-store.01.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf p.13, p.40, p.62-63; external/et-man/ET-SoC Errata.pdf p.84; external/core-et-main/hw/ip/shirecache/rtl/shirecache_pipe_sub_bank.sv:640-642

scp:scp.seq.remote-store.02.statement: mesh and target L3 slave: AXI AW/W across the mesh into the target's L3-slave port.
scp:scp.seq.remote-store.02.note: Time: 12 cycles per hop round trip

scp:scp.seq.remote-store.03.statement: target pipeline and data panels: Written like a local scratchpad write (step 4 of store_own); acknowledged back to the L3 slave.

scp:scp.seq.fill.01.statement: minion (hart 0 or hart 1) → bank: CSR 0x85F; for each line the bank issues a Mesh_Read of the source (L3, DRAM or a remote scratchpad; never the local L2, whose dirty data it ignores).
scp:scp.seq.fill.01.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.289-290; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf p.87

scp:scp.seq.fill.02.statement: bank pipeline, data panels: When the line returns, an SCP_Fill writes it into the local scratchpad row; no victim, no tag.

scp:scp.seq.atomic.01.statement: minion → UC block → mesh → home shire's L3 slave: Atomics to the scratchpad are not accepted from a neighbourhood directly ('must go to UC block'); through the self ID 0x7F they are a bus error.

scp:scp.seq.atomic.02.statement: home bank: data panel read, atomic block, data panel write: The sub-bank is held busy from the read through the write; the atomic block (a three-stage pipeline in the re-implementation RTL) computes the result; the response goes back as an ESR write over to_sys.
scp:scp.seq.atomic.02.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf p.17, p.36, p.40 §2.9; docs/findings/05-claims.md:427; external/core-et-main/hw/ip/shirecache/rtl/shirecache_pipe_atomic.sv:11 (three-stage pipeline, re-implementation RTL); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf p.17 ('atomic response data sent back as an ESR write to to_sys mesh')

scp:scp.seq.refresh.01.statement: (none): The scratchpad has no misses and no victims: every in-range address is a hit, and an out-of-range index returns an error (SC_PipeErr_ScpOpToNonEnRegion by p.25; the error list on p.111 names SC_PipeErr_ScpSetOutOfRange). Nothing is ever evicted.

scp:scp.seq.refresh.02.statement: (none): No refresh if the cells are static (SRAM-type) storage; the only standing cost is leakage, at most 19.6 mW per MB at 80 °C on this rail.
scp:scp.seq.refresh.02.note: Energy: leakage <= 19 nJ per byte-second at 80 °C

scp:scp.seq.refresh.03.statement: (none): No ECC scrubbing on ET-SoC-1 (a reserved bit for future chips).

load-hit.title: Load hit
load-hit.measured: 5.25 cycles load-to-use (measured); 17.3 pJ per 32 B flw.ps (random), 12.5 (zeros); 14.0 pJ per scalar flw

steps.block: integer pipeline ID stage; DCache replay queue; pre-S0 arbiter
steps.action: Reads the base register, checks the scoreboard, pre-allocates a replay-queue entry and bids for the DCache (the core is the lowest of six bidders).

circuit.el: Register-file read ports and flip-flops switch.

steps.action: Adds base + offset into the virtual address; the granted request (address, destination register, command, size) is registered into S1.

steps.block: TLB (8-entry latch RF); metadata array (4 tag latch RFs + valid flip-flops); 4 tag comparators; PMA; LRU read
steps.action: Set = PA[9:6] with the mode's forced MSBs; each of the 4 way-RFs puts out its 35-bit entry for that set in the same cycle; four 33-bit comparisons give a one-hot hit, encoded to the way; the PMA checks cacheability; the data-array row address {set, half, way} and the one block enable (addr[4:3]) are formed and captured by the LRAM's read-address register at the clock edge.

circuit.el: Tag latches are only read (their clocks stay gated off); their outputs pass a 16:1 select per bit; XNOR + AND trees switch; the LRAM address flip-flops toggle on the edge. Select and compare are generic; the registered read address is ET (rf_latch_1r_1w_reg.v:139-149).
circuit.kind_note: the registered read address is the ET latch-RF pattern, assumed for the LRAM; the silicon macro is asked

steps.block: data array: 1 of 4 blocks = 2 macros of 128 x 32 (LRAM); hit logic; LRU flip-flops
steps.action: In the enabled block the 7-bit row address selects the hit way's row; its 64 latches drive the read select to the 64-bit output, which is registered into the S2→S3 data registers; the other 3 blocks stay idle. The hit is confirmed and the set's LRU matrix is rewritten.

circuit.el: The stored latches are not disturbed; the row-select/mux-tree transistors and output wires switch in proportion to the data. No wordline boost, no bitline precharge, no sense amplifier if the macro is the latch-RF pattern (for latch arrays; the silicon macro is unknown).

steps.block: byte aligner, sign/zero extension, store bypass; integer register file
steps.action: Picks the 8 bytes out of the data registers, sign- or zero-extends, merges data from older stores still in S4/S5, and returns the value on s3_core_resp; the integer register file is written in WB.
A dependent load can read the value: 5 cycles issue to issue, measured as 5.25 in the unrolled chase on three cards; about 17 pJ per 32-byte load above idle on random data, including the instruction.
steps.latency: 5.25 cycles load-to-use (measured)
steps.energy: 17.3 pJ per 32 B flw.ps (random), 12.5 (zeros); 14.0 pJ per scalar flw

store-hit.title: Store hit
store-hit.measured: 23.0 pJ per 32 B fsw.ps (random); 25.5 pJ per scalar fsw

steps.action: Address, tag lookup and hit way exactly as a load; the store data is sent in the TAG stage (S1) and aligned into the S2 store-data register.
Reads the row being written (the store is a read-modify-write).
Merges the new bytes into the row read in S2.

Stores have the highest write priority. The per-block, per-half write enables and the 7-bit row address go to the macro; the write data was captured half a cycle earlier by the low-phase write-data latch; the decoded row's clock gate fires and that row's 64 latches turn transparent and take the new value.

circuit.el: One row clock gate + 64 latch cells per written block switch; the write-data latch toggles only on changed bits. The per-row gate and opposite-phase write latch are the ET latch-RF pattern (rf_latch_1r_1w_reg.v:88-136); transistor detail generic.
circuit.kind_note: the ET latch-RF pattern, assumed for the LRAM; the silicon macro is asked

steps.action: A store to an exclusive (clean) line has the miss handler rewrite its metadata to modified (one 35-bit latch-RF write).

steps.action: Keeps the store data one more cycle so a younger load of the same bytes in S3 gets it.

asks.title: Which of the chip's memories are not SRAM, and what cells they use
asks.question: Which memories the lab lead meant by "not using SRAM". The bitcell of the shire-cache macros (6T high-density, 8T, other), against the spec's "SRAM memory panels" (pdf p.48), the compiled 1PUHD/2PUHDRF macros (pdf p.51; Synopsys by inference), the datasheet's 140 MB of SRAM (pdf p.4) and core-et-main/AGENTS.md:609. Inside dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram: standard-cell latches placed like ET's rf_latch_1r_1w_reg library, or a custom or compiled latch array; transistors per bit; a static mux-tree read or a precharged read bitline. The HDBULT08 and HDBULT11 cell families and the "MMI (hand-tuned)" logic. Whether the L1 is latch RAM because the minion's LV region (400-620 mV by the firmware's limits, 0.517 V measured) is below the SRAM panels' 585 mV Vmin (our inference), and which other minion arrays (the VPU register file vpu_64x32_3r2w, the TLB) are latch arrays. The neighbourhood's instruction-cache data RAM (mbi, saduls0g4l1p512x144, the same 1PUHD family as the data panels) has the same open question.
asks.settles: The transistor views of every on-chip level: the L1's latch cell and read path (now the generic latch template) and the L2, L3 and scratchpad cell (now a generic 6T marked unknown); whether a shire-cache cell needs refresh (which would add a refresh step); the "why latches" caption confirmed or corrected.

asks.title: Datasheets (or .lib summaries) of the memory macros
asks.question: For saduls0g4l1p4096x144m4b4..., ...1024x116..., saculs0g4l2p1024x40... and dcache_128x32_1r1w_lram: rows x columns, column mux and internal banks (is m4b4 a 4:1 mux and 4 banks?), sense-amplifier type, bitline length, whether a global read bus is precharged, energy per read and per write at the running voltage, and leakage per macro. The same need as the hub's rung 19 (a cell library and netlist), narrowed to the memories.
asks.settles: The arrays and subarrays of the L1, L2, L3 and scratchpad drawn to scale instead of as illustrations; how many bitlines swing per access (half-select energy); the ledgers' energy split between array and periphery (now "not split").

asks.title: Where each cycle of a cache access goes
asks.question: Stage-by-stage latencies for an L1 hit (is it ID-EX-TAG-MEM-WB plus one cycle, with no S3 to EX bypass, and what costs hart 1 three extra cycles on every L1 miss?), an L2 hit (21 shire clocks inside and 26 outside, of which only about 6 are placed), a read-buffer hit (10), an L3 hit (the 110-cycle constant: 72.2 clock-scaled cycles + 61.4 ns, 109 at 600 MHz, against the spec's 34 + 30 shire clocks), and leaving and entering a shire for a remote scratchpad read (about 53 cycles), and the L3 home's extra cycles on a miss before the request leaves on To_Sys (the spec's 42 against 30 shire clocks).
asks.settles: Per-step cycle labels on every access of the L1, L2, L3 and scratchpad (now only the totals are measured).

asks.title: Which options of the open drop the silicon has
asks.question: The open core-et is the Erbium branch, and the spec v1.1 also documents later chips. Does the taped-out L1 carry parity or ECC, and can the minion arrays sleep? Is there an L2 hardware prefetcher (shire_cache_bank_l2hpf)? What is the read buffer built from (flip-flops in the re-implementation)? Are the v1.1 macros the taped-out ones? Does an L3 request pick its mesh lane by the home bank PA[12:11], as core-et-main's shirecache_mesh_master.sv:132-153 does?
asks.settles: Check bits drawn per L1 row or not; the prefetcher box drawn or removed; the read buffer's storage drawn; the L3 lane (and the correction to the chip tour's fact L103).

asks.title: The live shire-cache settings on these cards
asks.question: sc_pipe_ctl (esr_sc_ram_delay, esr_sc_zero_state_enable, the read-buffer enables) and shire_cache_ram_cfg1-4 (RM, RME, RA, WA, WPULSE, BC) on each card, at the 705 mV rail, and esr_sc_axi_qos (the priority the shire cache gives its memory requests). The open firmware never writes the trims, and the functional model's reset values are the spec's RM0 "650 mV nominal" row. One service-processor read of one shire per card, or an M-mode read, would do.
asks.settles: The panel access time drawn (2 cycles = 3.3 ns if 1:1); whether zero lines skip the panels on these cards; which read-assist and write-assist mode the cell animation shows.

asks.title: The DRAM part
asks.question: The Micron part number, die density, dies per package, and x16 or byte-mode channels. The firmware reads MR5 and MR8 at every boot and logs them (mem_controller_utils.c), but no log has been captured; a boot log or the card's BOM line settles it. The part's datasheet gives whatever it publishes of the internal organisation. With temperature derating off, also whether the packages stay under 85 C under load: a read of MR4 during a long run would show it.
asks.settles: The DRAM die scale drawn from the actual part instead of from the capacity and JEDEC; the generic die internals narrowed where the datasheet allows.

asks.title: What caps a shire at 128 B per cycle
asks.question: Own-scratchpad and L2 streams reach exactly 4.0 B per minion-cycle, half the four banks' 256 B. Sweep the tensor-load stride (64 B rotating banks, 256 B one bank rotating sub-banks, 1 KB one bank and one sub-bank) and 1 to 4 neighbourhoods per shire, and ask the design team which block is the limit.
asks.settles: Which block the diagram highlights when all 1,024 minions stream: sub-bank busy time, the response crossbar, the Fill FIFO, or the 256-bit minion port.

asks.title: How much the zero-line skip saves
asks.question: Clear esr_sc_zero_state_enable on one card for one L3 run (an M-mode ESR write) and compare zeros against random data; compare with the scratchpad, where the skip does not apply and zeros still save about 90 pJ per line on the SRAM rail on aifoundry2. Also write a line's quadwords to zero one at a time and time a later read, to see whether a partial write sets the zero bit.
asks.settles: Whether the L3 view shows the data panels idle for zero lines, and where the rest of the data-dependent energy sits (datapath, ECC, crossings).

asks.title: The Power Spec: which rail feeds the shire-cache logic
asks.question: Which rail feeds the shire-cache logic (pipeline, crossbars, queues, the high side of the VC FIFOs, the UC block) against the macros alone.
asks.settles: The rail band of each block and the split of SRAM-rail energy between arrays and logic.

asks.title: The minion's and the shire's floorplans
asks.question: Add the minion's partition (where the 8 LRAM macros, tag register files and TLB sit, and their area) and the placement of the banks, sub-banks and 96 macros relative to the mesh stop and the L3 slave ports.
asks.settles: The physical layer of the L1, L2 and L3: the distances an access travels inside the tile.

asks.title: The router pipeline
asks.question: The router pipeline per hop, which of the 9 main-NoC layers carry L3 requests and replies, and the flit width (the dimension order was measured on 29 September: l3.route).
asks.settles: The mesh-hop scale of the L3 and of the remote scratchpad.

asks.title: Where a DRAM load's last 63 cycles go, and the memory shire's rules
asks.question: How the up-to-63 cycles beyond the DRAM's own timing split between the L3 home's miss path and To_Sys crossings (about 12 cycles by the spec) and the memory shire's port and clock crossing, the controller's queues and the PHY (PA[9], the channel, is the memory shire's reset value, ms_regs.h:160; the row bits, PA[18] and up, are measured by one-bit flips on 3 cards; the bank bits PA[12:10] come from the programmed ADDRMAP, rung 33). Also: which traffic goes to each controller's two AXI ports; when a global atomic on a DRAM address is done in the memory shire's atomic unit rather than at the L3 home; the controller's total CAM depth; and where the memory shire's clock crossing sits.
asks.settles: The grey bar at the memory-shire scale, split between the L3 home and the memory shire; the controller's ports, CAM and atomic unit drawn from the design instead of from the init code.

asks.title: The card schematic: the package pairing and the DRAM's rails
asks.question: Already asked by the hub's row: the LPDDR4X package pairing. Also which card rail feeds the packages' VDD1 (1.8 V in JEDEC LPDDR4X).
asks.settles: The dashed pairing on the DRAM chip scale; the DRAM's supplies drawn complete.

asks.title: Current sensing below the regulators (not possible on silicon)
asks.question: The DRAM's off-rail 73 pJ/B, split between the memory shire's logic, PHY I/O, DRAM core and DRAM I/O, and refresh energy stay unmeasurable on the card.
asks.settles: The DRAM ledger's grey energy cells; they stay open.
