L09.statement: Each side strip (memory shires + LPDDR4x PHYs) is about 1.76 mm wide (1.74 and 1.80 mm for the two strips).

L101.statement: The mesh (routers, links, NetSpeed bridges) is on its own low-voltage rail at 0.485 V (0.484 V at the die).

L102.statement: Every shire's NoC port is 512 bits wide: one 64 B line per beat, single-beat only.

L103.statement: A shire has 4 to_l3 master and 4 L3 slave lanes to the mesh; the lane is chosen by PA[7:6], so lines i and i+4 share a lane (a 1 KB load puts 4 of its 16 lines on each).

L104.statement: The mesh routes in dimension order, and a request and its reply take opposite orders: a request goes x first, then y, and a reply y first, then x, on the logical map, so a reply retraces its request's route backwards. Measured on 29 September (E56) with sets of streams between shires chosen so that their streams share one directed link under one order and none under the other: 1 KB tensor loads, whose data travel as replies, fell to 0.54-0.77 of their bandwidth alone when they shared a link under y first and held at 1.00 when they shared one under x first; tensor stores, whose data travel as requests, showed the mirror (0.52-0.76 against 1.00). A shared link carried about 92 GB/s. The same on aifoundry1 card 1 (development), aifoundry3 (the frozen validation) and aifoundry2 (the same frozen test, run as a third card on the evening of 29 September), three passes each.
L104.source: tools/claims-v3/nocr/PREREG.md (frozen 29 Sep about 00:10 PDT, sha256 2472ab3e...; the sets: workloads/nocroute/meshmap.py, tools/claims-v3/nocr/sets.json); docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-nocr/raw/<card>/summary.json .r32.read and .r32.write: .verdict, .sets.<set>.rho_pooled (sets of 3 and 5 streams), .capacity_gbs_from_dropping_sets; docs/reports/data/2026-09-29-nocr/README.md
L104.note: Until 29 September this fact was inferred: the analyses assumed x first for every packet (as Chang infers), and every route on this page was drawn so (docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1b 'Routing'; heat-per-mm.script.js's route map, x first by default until 29 September: its `order` and the 'Routing order' toggle). What E56 saw is the data: a load's replies and a store's requests. That a load's own requests go x first and a store's acknowledgements y first follows if the order is set by the kind of packet; those small packets never slowed a set (each costs a link under 0.54 of a reply). On the die view x runs down the die's rows: a request first moves north or south, then east or west, and a reply first east or west.

L105.statement: Each mesh stop has 9 main-NoC routers (layers 0–8) plus one debug-NoC router; routers have 8 ports (H, E, S, W, N, I, J, K) with 4 VC slots each; route info, packet, sideband and data are parity-protected (no ECC).
L105.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1b rows 'Main-NoC layers', 'Router ports and VCs', 'Error protection' (etsoc_shire_other_esr.h:3877-3981; noc_esr.h)
L105.note: SYNTHESIS marks these 'U' (not independently re-verified); router-to-router flit width is unknown.

L11.statement: A minion-shire cell is about 13.8–13.95 mm²; the 34 minion shires take about 468–474 mm² (82–83% of the die).

L114.statement: Shire top level: the main NoC interface (ports to_l3 ×4, to_sys, l3_slave ×4, uc_to_l3, uc_to_sys, sys_slave) sits above the shire channel (shire cache with 4 banks, UC block, RBOX, ESR, I$ memories), which feeds the four neighbourhoods; clock domains CLOCK_NOC, SHIRE_CLOCK, NEIGH_CLOCK, with the PLL/DLL, sensors and debug NoC bridge below.
L114.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf p.5 Figure 1
L114.note: A logical block diagram, not a floorplan: no source gives where the four neighbourhoods and four banks sit physically inside the 3.7 mm tile.

L115.statement: Neighbourhood floorplan: two columns of four minions either side of a central 'neighbourhood channel'; left column M2, M0, M4, M6 and right column M3, M1, M5, M7 (north to south); all ports and the high-voltage region are at the north end, where it meets the shire channel.
L115.note: Placed to shorten the fast local messaging network: its tree edges 0–1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7 cross the channel and 0–2, 0–4, 4–6 are vertical neighbours (L116).

L116.statement: Inside a shire only the reduction-tree edges are fast: 68 cycles (113 ns) round trip for 28 pairs per shire (in every neighbourhood 0–1, 0–2, 0–4, 2–3, 4–5, 4–6, 6–7) and 114–115 cycles (190 ns) for all 468 others, in every pass on three cards.

L12.statement: Package is 45.0 × 45.0 mm (lid 44.8) with 2,494 balls and over 30,000 bumps to the die; the package drawing shows no die outline.
L12.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1a row 'Package' (citing external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.33 Fig. 9-1 and HC33 slide 20)

L120.statement: One temperature sensor and one process detector in each minion shire and the I/O shire (36 each), 8 voltage-monitor blocks with up to 128 remote sense points, read by five PVT controllers in the I/O shire.
L120.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.17 §1.6 and p.18 Figure 1-3, Table 1-6

L121.statement: 35 sensors are read: TS0–TS31 for the compute shires (TSn in shire n), TS32 master, TS33 spare, TS34 I/O; the PCIe shire has no sensor.

L123.statement: Per-shire on-die voltage at idle (34 minion shires): minion rail 517–521 mV, lows 513 (shires 0, 1, 2, 18) to 520, highs to 522; SRAM 703–707 mV; mesh 483–486 mV.

L28.statement: The PCIe shire holds two independent PCI Express controllers and an 8-lane PCIe physical interface (Gen4, up to 25.78 Gb/s per lane).
L28.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.8 §1.2; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.4 §1

L29.statement: The I/O shire holds a Maxion neighbourhood of four ET-Maxion cores, another 4 MB L2/L3, the service processor with its ROM and 1 MB scratchpad SRAM, a hardware root of trust, USB, I2C, SPI and UARTs; the five PVT controllers also sit in it.
L29.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.8 §1.2 and p.17 §1.6

L46.statement: Of the 91-cycle memory-shire constant (152 ns), the DRAM chip accounts for about 25–28 cycles (activate tRCD 11 cycles = 18 ns, 19.3 ns read latency, one or two 4.3 ns bursts); at most ~63–66 cycles (~105–110 ns) are the memory shire itself: controller queue, PHY and the crossings between the 933 MHz DDR clock and the mesh.
L46.note: 'At most' because each hop further out moves 12 cycles from the constant into the mesh legs.

L47.statement: Each memory shire drives two 16-bit LPDDR4X channels (16 in all, four external LPDDR4X chips of four 16-bit channels = 64 bits each); two memory shires share each 64-bit LPDDR4X device, at up to 4,266 Mb/s per pin.
L47.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf p.17 §1.5; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.30 §7 and §7.1
L47.note: The manuals differ on controllers: PRM p.17 'two memory controllers that each have a 16-bit LPDDR4X channel'; DS p.30 'two 16-bit LPDDR4X physical interfaces sharing a single 32-bit controller'. docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:286 follows the PRM (2 uMCTL2 per memshire).

L48.statement: Each memory shire has a 512-bit NoC memory port; the datasheet gives the NoC side a maximum of 32 GB/s per memory shire, almost twice the sustained LPDDR4X throughput behind it.
L48.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf p.30 §7.1.1 and §7.1.1.1

L88.statement: A random bit moved 1 mm over free links at 0.485 V: mesh rail 36.1 [35.2–37.0] (aifoundry2), 35.8 [35.1–36.5] (aifoundry3), 38.1 [26.3–49.9] fJ (aifoundry1 card 1); board power 46.7, 44.4, 51.1 fJ.
L88.note: 36.2 fJ is the two-card (E32) mesh-rail value: 24.6 data + 11.7 fixed.

L92.statement: A per-reader tensor load over one hop on a link it uses alone moved at least 46.8 GB/s: at least 117 B per 400 MHz NoC cycle per link direction, more than one 512-bit layer (25.6 GB/s); the link was not saturated.
L92.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/SYNTHESIS.md §1b row 'Measured data per link direction' (docs/reports/data/2026-09-23-energy-manual/catalogue.json wire/hop1)
L92.note: Card not stated in SYNTHESIS (E27 ran on aifoundry2 and aifoundry3).

board.regulators.statement: Regulators: minion and NoC share a TI TPSM831D31 (minion on a 3-phase output, 120 A max; NoC single-phase, 40 A max); the SRAM rail is an LTM4680 (60 A max).

chip.compute-array.statement: Typically 32 minion shires form the compute array and one more is the management (master) shire; the datasheet calls this a software convention, all minion shires being identical. The 34th is a yield-recovery spare, powered down in production.
chip.compute-array.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.486 (§15.3: 'the 34th shire will be designated as a powered down yield recovery spare')

chip.cores-total.statement: The ET-SoC-1 has 1,093 RISC-V cores: 1,088 ET-Minions, 4 ET-Maxions and 1 Minion-based service processor.
chip.cores-total.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1 Product Overview); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.7 (§1)

chip.die-area.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md:513; docs/findings/01-resources.md:234 (R14: Hot Chips 33 slide 20; IEEE Micro 42(3) p.37)

chip.die-dims.statement: Die about 25.6-25.8 mm east-west by 22.1-22.2 mm north-south (width/height 1.15-1.17), from the published die plot scaled to 570 mm²; the shire grid spans about 86% of the die's width, the rest being the memory shires and their DRAM PHYs down each side (about 1.76 mm per side).
chip.die-dims.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-24-wire-energy/research/geometry/pitch.json, `scale_from_570mm2.A_black_layout_region` and `.B_symmetric_bottom` (`die_w_mm`, `die_h_mm`, `grid_w_mm`, `memshire_col_w_mm`); heat-per-mm page §'How long is a hop'
chip.die-dims.note: Pixel measurement of a die plot; depends on what the 570 mm² covers. Use for proportions only.

chip.harts.statement: Software sees 2,048 harts on the 32 compute shires: hartid = shire × 64 + minion × 2 + thread (shire = hartid >> 6, neighbourhood = (hartid mod 64) >> 4, minion = hartid >> 1, thread = hartid & 1).

chip.hop-pitch.statement: Shire tile pitch 3.73 mm east-west and 3.70 mm north-south, so one mesh hop is about 3.72 mm (3.64-3.74 over three readings).
chip.hop-pitch.note: Kind A (estimate from the die plot) in the claims index.

chip.io-shire.statement: The I/O shire holds the Maxion neighbourhood (4 Maxions) with a shared L2/L3 cache, the service processor with ROM and 1 MB SRAM, a hardware root of trust, five PVT controllers and the peripherals (USB, I2C, SPI, UART, eMMC).
chip.io-shire.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.6, PVT controllers in the I/O shire)
chip.io-shire.note: Sources disagree on the Maxions' cache: the datasheet (pdf p.5) and PRM (pdf p.486) say 4 MB; the Shire Cache Specification (pdf p.22) says 'the IOShire has a cache total of 1 MB'.

chip.master-shire-id.statement: The master shire (which runs the master-minion firmware and schedules kernels) is shire 32 in the firmware; its 2.5 MB scratchpad at 0x9000_0000 holds the firmware's host-interface buffers.
chip.master-shire-id.note: layout.h:45 also reserves MASTER_SHIRE_COMPUTE_HARTS 32; minion_configuration.h:53 MM_MASTER_SHIRE_NEIGH_NUM 2.

chip.maxions.statement: Four ET-Maxion 64-bit RISC-V single-threaded superscalar out-of-order cores sit in the I/O shire with a system bus and coherency hub; they may be used for management tasks.
chip.maxions.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4 (§1) and pdf p.18 (§2.5.2)

chip.memshires.statement: Eight memory shires, four on the east side and four on the west side of the die, each driving two 16-bit LPDDR4X channels: 16 channels in all.
chip.memshires.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30 (§7); external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.5)

chip.pcie-shire.statement: The PCIe shire contains two independent dual-mode PCIe controllers and an 8-lane PCIe Gen4 PHY, factory-configured as an endpoint; the dev card exposes a Gen4 x8 host interface.
chip.pcie-shire.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and pdf p.17 (§2.3, Figure 2-7)

chip.process.statement: TSMC 7 nm, over 24 billion transistors, 89 mask layers (Esperanto, Hot Chips 33 and IEEE Micro 2022).
chip.process.note: External, published by the vendor; not checked on these cards.

chip.service-processor.statement: The service processor is a single ET-Minion core (one hart, no vector or tensor extension, no shire cache) in the I/O shire, with its own ROM and 1 MB scratchpad SRAM; it boots the chip, runs the power/clock governor and answers the host's management commands.
chip.service-processor.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1) and pdf p.18 (§2.4); external/et-man/ET Introduction.pdf, pdf p.7 ('Service Processor is a minion without vector/tensor extensions')
chip.service-processor.page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

chip.spare-shire-id.statement: The spare shire is bit 33 of the firmware's 34-shire mask; the NoC reconfiguration code remaps virtual shire IDs when the spare displaces a shire.

clock.design.statement: Design clocks: shire PLL output 1,000 MHz; a step clock of 400-1,000 MHz from PLL4 in the I/O shire; NoC clock 500 MHz from PLL2 in the I/O shire; reference oscillators 24 MHz and 100 MHz; the RISC-V mtime timer ticks at 10 MHz.
clock.design.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.12 (Table 2); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.16 (§2.2.6), p.22 (§5.1.1), p.29 (§6.6.2.1)

clock.dvfs-limits.statement: Firmware DVFS limits: minion 300-800 MHz, NoC 300-500 MHz; the minion PLL table covers 300-1,400 MHz in 25 MHz steps.
clock.dvfs-limits.page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

dram.capacity.statement: 32 GB of LPDDR4X on these V3 cards (Micron part): 2 GB per channel; the chip supports 8 to 32 GB.
dram.capacity.source: external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.1; docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:289; external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.342 and p.552; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30

dram.channels.statement: 16 LPDDR4X channels of 16 bits (256 bits in all): each memory shire drives two channels, and four LPDDR4X packages of four channels (64 bits each) sit on the card.
dram.channels.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.17 (§1.5); external/et-man/ET-PCIe-Dev-Card-V3.pdf, pdf p.3; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.4
dram.channels.note: The datasheet (pdf p.30) says two 16-bit PHYs share one 32-bit controller per memory shire; the firmware programs two uMCTL2 controller instances per memory shire (docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:286-287).

dram.controller-policy.statement: Controller configuration as programmed: open page, no auto-precharge, no power-down or self-refresh, no automatic ZQ, ECC off; tRCD = tRP = 18.2 ns, read latency 19.3 ns. DDR controller registers are service-processor only.

dram.counters.statement: Each memory shire has a perf monitor with a 40-bit cycle counter (933 MHz) and two event counters; the firmware sets them to count mesh reads and writes, which U-mode can sample through syscall 10.

dram.leg.statement: Past the L3, the DRAM leg costs 91 + 12 × hops(home shire, memory shire) cycles; about 25 of the 91 are the DRAM chip (activate 11, read and burst 14) and about 66 the memory shire. Only 25-28 of a ~300-cycle DRAM load are the DRAM's own timing.
dram.leg.source: docs/et-soc1-notes.md:166; docs/reports/data/2026-09-19-memprobe-aifoundry2/summary.json `decomp.ms_const`; cards.json `ms_const` (90-91 on three cards); docs/findings/05-claims.md:404

dram.pkg-pairing.statement: Which two memory shires share each LPDDR4X device is not documented: the datasheet says only that two memory shires communicate with each 64-bit device. The diagram pairs neighbouring memory shires on each side (0 and 1, 2 and 3, 4 and 5, 6 and 7), after the block diagram's two LPDDR4X blocks per side, on the inferred die placement.
dram.pkg-pairing.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.30 (§7: 'Two Memshires communicate with each 64-bit LPDDR4X memory device') and p.15 (Figure 2-6, fact L23)

dram.rate-card.statement: The firmware hard-codes the 933 MHz DDR configuration on every card (controller clock 933 MHz, DRAM clock 1,866 MHz, 3,733 MT/s); telemetry reads mhz.ddr = 933 in every sample.

dram.row-bits.statement: Inside a channel: bank PA[12:10], column PA[17:13] (plus PA[5:1] within the line), row PA[18] and up (PA[34:18]); 8 banks, 2 KB page, one rank per channel.
dram.row-bits.note: Row/bank bits measured with one address bit flipped; the controller's ADDRMAP decode is the research agent's inference.

e-awake.statement: An awake minion (addi loop) costs about 2 mW (1.87 mW one hart, 3.02 mW both harts, aifoundry2); 5.1 / 6.6 pJ per instruction pooled over three cards.
e-awake.note: Keeping 1,024 minions awake for a second is 2-3.1 J, against 36 J for the card at 80 C.

e-flip-model.statement: Tensor unit energy by RTL event (fitted on aifoundry2): 3.18 fJ per register bit clocked, 0.025 per multiplier-tree net toggle, 0.80 per other net toggle, 15.5 per operand-word bit; 1.8 mW per minion of state machines. A random tile prices at 27.2 W on 1,024 minions.
e-flip-model.note: A fit (E17); 14 structured matrices predicted to 0.9 W rms before they ran.

e-fmadd-ps.statement: 8-lane vector multiply-add fmadd.ps: 27.1 pJ [26.4-28.9] on zeros, 55.8 [53.8-57.0] on random data, 7.0 pJ per lane-MAC (6.3-6.4 with the instruction issue taken out); 16 flops.
e-fmadd-ps.note: Per card random: a2 55.6, a3 56.2, a1c1 55.4. The vector lane is ~10% above the tensor unit's 5.8 pJ per multiply-add.

e-tfma-fp32.statement: TensorFMA fp32 random: 5.782 pJ per multiply-add [5.347-6.133] above idle, all 1,024 minions; per card a2 5.920, a3 5.369, a1c1 6.058.
e-tfma-fp32.source: manual.json: tensor.bars.fp32_randn (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/03-instructions.md:45
e-tfma-fp32.note: Loaded (idle included, aifoundry2 at 80 C): 13.84 pJ per MAC. 546 cycles per 16x16x16 op. Launched at 80 C (a3 at 57 C); amendment C2 offset applies.

e-tfma-fp32-zeros.statement: TensorFMA fp32 zeros: 0.273 pJ per multiply-add [0.141-0.445] above idle, all 1,024 minions; per card a2 0.403, a3 0.163, a1c1 0.251.
e-tfma-fp32-zeros.source: manual.json: tensor.bars.fp32_zeros (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/03-instructions.md:43
e-tfma-fp32-zeros.note: Zeros clock nothing: the lane clock is withheld when an operand word is zero.

e-tfma-int8.statement: TensorFMA int8 random: 0.295 pJ per multiply-add [0.260-0.317] above idle, all 1,024 minions; per card a2 0.313, a3 0.262, a1c1 0.309.
e-tfma-int8.source: manual.json: tensor.bars.int8_randn (mean, lo, hi, per_card); docs/energy-manual/03-instructions.md:51
e-tfma-int8.note: int8 is about 19x cheaper per MAC than fp32 (E38: 18.9-20.5 by card). 318 cycles per 16x16x64 op.

fw.grey-cells.statement: In the firmware's maps the four cells that hold no compute shire are: logical (0, 3), shire 32, the master; (5, 3), shire 33, the spare; (0, 4), the PCIe shire ('pcie0' in the bridge map); and (0, 5), the I/O shire ('io0'). On this die view that puts the master in the north cell and the spare in the south one, with PCIe then I/O east of the master.
fw.grey-cells.note: To confirm on the cards: time a counter read on shire 32 from each compute shire (the hub's rung exp-mesh-stops).

hot-cost.statement: One contended global atomic (amoaddg.w on one line, 1,024 minions): the bank retires one every 10.00 cycles, about 60 M/s for the whole chip; spread over 32 lines, one per shire, 0.31 cycles and 1,919 M/s: 32x.
hot-cost.note: The atomic itself is fair: every shire gets 0.998-1.004 of an even split, the host included.
hot-cost.page: One hot line stops a shire

idle-rails.statement: Where idle goes at 73 C (aifoundry2): minions 11.05 W (35%), SRAM 2.00 W (6%), mesh 3.64 W (11%), no rail sensor (PCIe, DDR PHY, I/O shire, regulators) 15.10 W (48%); board 31.79 W. aifoundry1-c1 at 73 C: 15.96 / 3.05 / 5.83 / 17.87, board 42.71 W.
idle-rails.source: manual.json: rest.rails_73c (minion 11.05, sram 2.00, noc 3.64, unsensed 15.10, board 31.79); docs/energy-manual/01-at-rest.md:29
idle-rails.note: The unsensed ~15 W is the largest single component of idle on every card and cannot be split with any instrument here.

l3.latency.statement: L3 hit: 110 + 12 cycles per mesh hop between the requesting shire and the line's home shire (fitted 110.5 + 11.99 on three cards); 159-169 cycles (265-282 ns) on average depending on the requesting shire.

lat-l1.statement: L1 data cache hit: 5.25 cycles load-to-use (8.8 ns at 600 MHz); the same on three cards (per-pass ranges 5.247-5.259).
lat-l1.note: Only 512 B of L1 per hart: the firmware puts the L1 in scratchpad mode before every launch.

lat-scp-own.statement: The shire's own L2 scratchpad: 47 cycles (78 ns), the same SRAM, latency and bandwidth as the L2 cache.

lat-scp-remote.statement: Another shire's scratchpad: 99.84 + 12.00 cycles per mesh hop at 600 MHz (112-220 cycles, 186-366 ns over 1-10 hops); all 124 points within 1 cycle, a->b equals b->a within 0.032 cycles.
lat-scp-remote.note: Clock model (aifoundry2, 18 Sep): 66 minion cycles + 56 ns + 20 ns per hop.

mesh-bit-mm-free.statement: A random bit per mm on free links, mesh rail at 0.485 V: 37 fJ (25 of it data-dependent); on board power 47 fJ. Dally's rule of thumb is ~100 fJ/b-mm.
mesh-bit-mm-free.note: Per card, mesh rail: a2 36.1, a3 35.8, a1c1 38.1 fJ; board 46.7, 44.4, 51.1 fJ (99% intervals in 05-claims). Scaled to 0.9 V the data cost is 85-105 fJ.

mesh-hop-lat.statement: Each mesh hop adds 12 cycles round trip at 600 MHz (20 ns): L3 11.99, remote scratchpad 12.00, TensorSend 12.01-12.02 cycles per hop on every card.
mesh-hop-lat.note: 20 ns at either clock (16 cycles at 800 MHz): a NoC-clock cost.

mesh.clock.statement: The NoC runs at 400 MHz on these cards (every telemetry sample). The design's NoC clock is 500 MHz (from PLL2 in the I/O shire), and the firmware's DVFS table allows 300-500 MHz.
mesh.clock.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl (and horace2-, thermal-telemetry.jsonl: 3,681 samples, 20 Sep), field `mhz.noc`; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.12 (Table 2, clk__noc); external/et-platform/device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:134-135
mesh.clock.cards_txt: aifoundry2 (aifoundry3 is set to 400 MHz by its boot service)
mesh.clock.card: aifoundry2 (aifoundry3 set to 400 MHz by its boot service)

mesh.grid.statement: The NoC is an 8 × 6 grid of mesh stops: 34 minion shires, 1 PCIe shire, 1 I/O shire and 8 memory shires; the four memory shires on each side leave the grid's corners empty, so there are 44 mesh stops.
mesh.grid.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.21 (§4 ET-SoC-1 Mesh Network on Chip)

mesh.single-attach.statement: Each shire meets the mesh at a single point: minion 31 of each shire gives the same round trips as minion 0.
mesh.single-attach.source: on-chip communication page §'What the numbers say'

mesh.voltage.statement: NoC rail: set point 485 mV, 484-485 mV on die (per-shire 483-486 mV at idle).
mesh.voltage.source: docs/reports/data/2026-09-20-power-aifoundry2/horace-telemetry.jsonl (and horace2-, thermal-telemetry.jsonl: 3,681 samples, 20 Sep), fields `reg_mv.noc`, `die_mv.noc`; docs/findings/05-claims.md:41

minion.combine-free.statement: Combining on receive (fp32/int32 add, max, min) adds 0 cycles to a round trip.

minion.etlink-width.statement: A minion's ET-Link request and response interfaces are 256 bits wide: the neighbourhood's request datapath is 256 bits, up-converted to 512 bits only at its output to the shire, and a 512-bit response reaches the minion as two 256-bit halves.
minion.etlink-width.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.15 (§4.3: 'The data size of the request datapath is 256 bits' ... 'a final up-conversion to 512 bits') and p.23 (§4.4.3: 'the Minion response interface is 256-bit wide')

minion.isa.statement: The ET-Minion is a dual-threaded (2 harts), in-order, single-issue RV64IMFC core with Zicsr and Zifencei and machine/supervisor/user modes; kernels run in U-mode.
minion.isa.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion Description.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.7 (§2.1.1); external/et-man/ET Introduction.pdf, pdf p.7

minion.l1-firmware.statement: The firmware puts every minion's L1 in scratchpad mode before each launch, leaving each hart 512 B of data cache (2 sets × 4 ways × 64 B).

minion.l1-modes.statement: Three L1 modes (mcache_control D1Split, ScpEnable): shared (both harts, all sets); split (hart 0 sets 0-7, hart 1 sets 14-15); scratchpad (hart 0 sets 12-13, hart 1 sets 14-15, sets 0-11 become a 3 KB = 48-line tensor scratchpad).
minion.l1-modes.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.245-246 (§8.3.1, Table 8.4)
minion.l1-modes.note: The Minion Overview slide draws split mode as 2 KB per hart; the PRM table is followed here.

minion.l1d.statement: Each minion has a private 4 KB L1 data cache: 16 sets × 4 ways × 64 B lines, not coherent with any other cache, writing back whole 64-byte lines.
minion.l1d.source: external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.1 (slide 2); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.9 (§2.1.1.5)

minion.miss-handlers.statement: Two miss handlers per minion, so at most 2 outstanding cacheable line misses; tensor loads keep up to 4 L2 transfers in flight; there is no prefetcher.

minion.no-divide.statement: No hardware divide or square root in U-mode: fdiv.ps and fsqrt.ps trap, as do sine, reciprocal square root, 64-bit float conversion and reading the cycle CSR; 161 of the instructions tried execute in U-mode, 13 trap.

minion.one-ready-bit.statement: The hardware keeps one peer-to-peer ready bit per minion, not one per partner: a minion receiving from two TensorSend partners at once hangs its hart permanently (the card then needs a reset).
minion.one-ready-bit.note: sys_emu tracks every partner separately and does not reproduce the hang.

minion.power-awake.statement: An awake minion running an integer loop on one hart costs about 1.9 mW (both harts about 3.0 mW); on a random-data fp32 matmul a minion draws about 26.5 mW above idle (aifoundry2).

minion.sleep-unused.statement: The minion's sleep and isolation ports (nsleepin, iso_enable, nsleepout) are marked 'not used'; in the open Erbium RTL they are tied off and no firmware drives them. Idle cores are clock-gated, not power-gated.
minion.sleep-unused.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion Description.pdf, pdf p.7 (interfaces table); docs/findings/05-claims.md:177-179
minion.sleep-unused.page: The DVFS loop and its leakage

minion.tenb-tenc.statement: TenB is virtually 16 registers × 64 B (1 KiB), physically much smaller, and only streams loaded data to a consumer; TenC is 16 × 64 B (1 KiB) of int32 accumulators visible only to integer tensor multiplies.
minion.tenb-tenc.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.264

minion.tensor-csrs.statement: Tensor instructions are CSR writes that run asynchronously: tensor_fma 0x801, tensor_load 0x83F, tensor_load_l2 (TensorLoadL2Scp) 0x85F, tensor_quant 0x806, tensor_store 0x87F, tensor_reduce 0x800 (TensorSend/Recv/Broadcast/Reduce), tensor_wait 0x830.
minion.tensor-csrs.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.272-274 (§9.3)

minion.tensor-hart0.statement: Only hart 0 of a minion may issue tensor instructions; hart 1 may only issue TensorLoadL2Scp, TensorWait and tensor_coop accesses.
minion.tensor-hart0.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.264

minion.tensor-shape.statement: A TensorFMA computes C[M][N] += A[M][K] · B[K][N] with M, N ≤ 16 and K ≤ 64 / (bytes per element): A from the L1 scratchpad, B streamed through TenB, C accumulated in hart 0's vector registers (int8 in TenC). One fp32 op is 4,096 multiply-adds.
minion.tensor-shape.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.264 (§9); docs/et-soc1-notes.md:292-294

minion.tensorfma-546.statement: With A and B both in the L1 scratchpad a 16×16×16 fp32 TensorFMA takes 546 cycles (fp16 546, int8 318), identical for every data pattern.

minion.tensorload.statement: TensorLoad reads up to 16 rows of 64 contiguous bytes (64 B aligned, row stride in x31) from memory into consecutive L1-scratchpad lines, bypassing the L1 data cache; a mask can skip rows.
minion.tensorload.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.273 and p.275 (§9.3.1, TensorLoad)

minion.vec-peak.statement: The tensor instructions run on the vector unit's own lanes: each of the 8 lanes holds the FMA (TxFMA) and the two int8 multiply-add (IMA/TIMA) units, and state machines in the VPU sequence the multi-cycle tensor operations on them. An 8-lane fmadd.ps does 16 FLOP per cycle, the same fp32 peak as TensorFMA.
minion.vec-peak.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.8 (§2.1.1.2: TxFMA, a pair of IMA units and 'Finite state machines that generate long sequences of vector operations to implement multi-cycle tensor operations'); external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf, pdf p.11 (§2: TXFMA and two TIMA units per lane); scripts/ridge-points.py:46, 51 (fp32 TensorFMA and vec32 fmadd.ps, per_cycle 16 each)

minion.vector-rate.statement: A simple vector-FMA loop reaches only about 1.5 lane-FMAs per cycle per minion; the best published vector-unit matmul is 2.94 TFLOP/s at 650 MHz (FOSDEM 2026), against the tensor unit's 9.5.

minion.vpu.statement: The vector unit has 8 identical 32-bit lanes in lockstep; the 32 FP registers f0-f31 are 256 bits wide (8 × fp32) per hart. Each lane has one FMA unit (one fp32 or two fp16 multiply-adds per cycle), two integer multiply-add units (four int8 multiply-accumulates each), one integer unit and one transcendental unit (exp2, log2, reciprocal).
minion.vpu.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.8 (§2.1.1.2); external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf, pdf p.11 (§2) and p.33 (§2.2.5.2: 16 TIMA lanes); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.2 (slide 3)

minion.vpu-pipeline.statement: The VPU pipeline has eight stages.

minion.vpu-regs.statement: Each lane's register file holds 64 × 32-bit entries (32 per thread), so each hart has 32 vector registers of 32 bytes; 8 mask registers of 8 bits.
minion.vpu-regs.source: external/core-et/docs/Minion VPU Specification.pdf, pdf p.11; external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.8-9
minion.vpu-regs.unit: vector registers per hart (32 B each)

neigh.composition.statement: A neighbourhood is 8 minions sharing a 32 KB L1 instruction cache (128 sets × 4 ways × 64 B), two L0 micro-I-caches (each shared by 4 minions, 16 fully associative 512-bit entries) and a 12-counter PMU.
neigh.composition.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.11-13 (§2.1.2); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.3 (slide 4)

neigh.coop-tload.statement: Cooperative TensorLoad: identical tensor-load requests from minions (across the neighbourhoods of a shire) are synchronised and coalesced into one memory request; cooperative TensorStore combines pairs or quads of minions writing one line.
neigh.coop-tload.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.273-274 (§9.3.1.1, §9.3.5.1); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.3

neigh.fln-edges.statement: The fast local messaging network links minions within a neighbourhood only along the reduction tree: 0-1, 0-2, 0-4, 2-3, 4-5, 4-6, 6-7.
neigh.fln-edges.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.26 (§4.7 Fast Local Messaging Network)

neigh.fln-latency-spec.statement: Messages on the fast local network see a 3-cycle response-path latency and take priority over regular fill responses; every other message leaves the neighbourhood and returns through the shire crossbar.

neigh.pmu.statement: The neighbourhood PMU implements 12 counters: 6 shared by the even harts (hart 0 of each minion) and 6 by the odd harts; mcycle and minstret read 0.
neigh.pmu.source: external/et-man/ET Programmer's Reference Manual.pdf, pdf p.10 and p.12 (§1.3, §1.3.2)

pcie.h2d.statement: Host to device, DMA only (the runtime's host-side copy replaced by a no-op, the analogue of pinned memory), 256 MB per copy: 12.47 [12.39, 12.55] GB/s on aifoundry2, 12.60 [12.55, 12.65] GB/s on aifoundry3, 12.46 [12.41, 12.50] GB/s on aifoundry1-c1 (mean of 5 runs [99% interval]): 12.46-12.60 GB/s, 79-80% of the link's 15.75 GB/s.

pcie.negotiated.statement: The link trained at 16.0 GT/s x8 on all three cards in every run (sysfs current_link_speed and current_link_width): PCIe Gen4 x8, 15.75 GB/s per direction after 128b/130b coding.

scp.size.statement: Each shire's scratchpad is 2.5 MB (0x280000 in the firmware); 80 MB over the 32 compute shires.
scp.size.page: Hand it to the next shire: on-chip relay vs DRAM

shire.bank-queues.statement: Per bank: a 64-entry request queue (up to 21 entries reserved for L3-slave requests), an 8-entry read buffer and a 32-entry write-around coalescing buffer; L3-slave requests take priority over local L2 requests.
shire.bank-queues.source: docs/research/counters-and-dram.md:458-465; external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.9 (coalescing buffer, 32 entries per bank) and pdf p.36 (arbitration)
shire.bank-queues.page: One hot line stops a shire

shire.cache-geometry.statement: The shire cache is 4 MB: 4 banks × 1 MB, each bank 4 sub-banks; L2 and L3 are 4-way set-associative, 64-byte lines, write-back and write-allocate, with SECDED ECC on tags, data and state.
shire.cache-geometry.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.8-9 (§1.1: 'The POR for the first SoC is 4M/Shire, 4 banks/Shire, 4 sub-banks/bank'); external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.13 (§2.1.3.1)

shire.clock.statement: Each minion shire has its own PLL; the shire cache and minions run on the shire clock (the neighbourhood clock is the same clock shifted 180°), outside the NoC's clock domain. Design value 1,000 MHz.
shire.clock.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.4 and pdf p.12 (Table 2: o_clkpll_shire, o_clkpll_neigh)
shire.clock.note: Measured consequence: on-chip latencies (L1, L2, own scratchpad) stay fixed in cycles when the clock moves, while L3 and DRAM are fixed in ns.

shire.composition.statement: A minion shire is 4 neighbourhoods = 32 minions = 64 harts, a four-bank 4 MB shared L2/L3/scratchpad cache, a mesh stop, a crossbar between them, and an uncacheable (UC) block with fast local barriers, fast credit counters, inter-processor interrupts and global atomics.
shire.composition.source: external/et-man/ET Preliminary Datasheet Rev 1.0.pdf, pdf p.5 (§2.1); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.4 (slide 5)

shire.crossbar.statement: A full request crossbar joins the 4 neighbourhoods and the RBOX to the 4 banks and the UC block; each bank has five 512-bit L2 input ET-Link buses, one 512-bit L3 input bus from the NoC, and two outputs toward the NoC: 'To L3' and 'To System' (main memory).

shire.neigh-link.statement: The 8 minions of a neighbourhood share one 512-bit ET-Link bus to the shire cache and UC block; responses reach a minion over a 256-bit bus (a 512-bit line takes two cycles).
shire.neigh-link.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.11 (§3.2); external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Neigborhood-MAS.pdf, pdf p.22-23

shire.partition-m0.statement: Mode M0, the reset mode and the one these cards run: per shire 2.5 MB scratchpad, 512 KB L2, 1 MB L3 slice; over 32 shires 80 MB scratchpad, 16 MB L2, 32 MB L3.
shire.partition-m0.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET-Shire-Cache-Specification.pdf, pdf p.21-22 (Tables 6-7, 'The chip will come out of reset in mode M0'); external/core-et/rtl/shire/esr/esr_cache_bank.v:106 ('default cache config mode = M0'); external/et-man/ET Minion Overview.pdf, pdf p.4

shire.voltage-domains.statement: A shire spans several voltage domains separated by level shifters and FIFOs: minions on the low-voltage minion rail, the SRAM arrays (shire cache, and the I-cache data memory, placed in the shire channel because it must run at high voltage) on the SRAM rail, the mesh stop on the NoC rail.
shire.voltage-domains.source: external/core-et/docs/CORE-ET Minion Shire Description.pdf, pdf p.4, p.10 (§3.1) and p.18 (§5); docs/research/why-low-power.md:23-28 (R6)

sync-shire-barrier.statement: Shire barrier (fast local barrier + credits, 32 minions, all 32 shires at once): 233 cycles (388 ns); 232.5-232.7 on the three cards.

temp-sensors.statement: 35 temperature sensors on the die (34 minion shires + the I/O shire, one per tile of the 6x6 grid except PCIe), 12-bit (0.061 C) in hardware; the host sees one 34-shire mean in whole degrees plus peak-hold extremes.

ts-rt-fln.statement: TensorSend round trip, 32 B register to register inside a shire: 68 cycles (113 ns) on the 7 fast-network tree edges of each neighbourhood, 114-115 cycles (190 ns) for every other pair.
ts-rt-fln.source: docs/findings/05-claims.md:380; docs/reports/2026-09-18-et-soc1-on-chip-communication.html "Inside a shire, only the tree edges are fast"
ts-rt-fln.note: Same pairs and same cycles in every pass on all three cards.
